description:
PROBLEM
After attempt 20260713T062233-4a0585c0 failed, the managed worker launched post-attempt bead-lifecycle triage as Codex PID 1130622. During that live provider call, ddx work status --json reported active_work.count=1 but bead_ids=[] and no provider_children, even though the prompt was explicitly classifying ddx-aa6cc320. A slow or leaked classifier is therefore indistinguishable from an idle worker and can block the single queue worker indefinitely after the implementation lease is already released.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3623-3625 clears the attempt liveness record immediately when the implementation attempt returns. The later parking path at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:4103-4117 releases the claim and invokes runPostAttemptTriage without publishing a candidate-scoped phase. runPostAttemptTriage at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:640-653 calls the hook directly with the long-lived loop context and no operation deadline or descendant cleanup. cli/internal/agent/triage_hook.go:109-123 dispatches the model provider, so any provider child created there is outside the attempt watchdog and absent from status.

PROPOSED FIX
- Publish transient candidate-scoped post_attempt_triage liveness before dispatch, heartbeat it with provider-child metadata, and keep it explicitly lease-free.
- Add a configurable bounded post-attempt triage deadline with a conservative default; on expiry append a structured post_attempt_triage_timeout event, preserve the original report, and continue the watch loop.
- Establish a provider-process baseline and terminate/reap only descendants introduced by the triage hook on success, malformed output, error, timeout, and cancellation.
- Clear transient triage state on every return while preserving the existing fail-open report semantics and event ordering.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx workers continue attempting claims and dispatches while /tmp is already near inode exhaustion, so one failing attempt can cascade into many ENOSPC failures. On 2026-07-08, DDx and Cayce workers repeatedly failed shell startup with `ENOSPC: no space left on device, mkdir /tmp/claude-501/...`; manual stale cleanup restored progress immediately. Cleanup exists, but it is not escalated aggressively when inode use crosses a critical threshold.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1664 runs cleanup at worker startup and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2044 runs cleanup pre-claim, but the cleanup pass is generic and does not escalate based on inode high-water state.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:821-825 uses a fixed default scratch min age, so even obvious DDx-owned scratch may survive until the age threshold despite active resource pressure.
cli/internal/agent/execution_resources.go:250-267 checks roots after cleanup but does not trigger an aggressive DDx-owned scratch cleanup mode when inode use is critically high.

PROPOSED FIX
Add an inode high-water cleanup mode before claim and before dispatch: if a checked temp root has inode usage above a critical threshold or free inodes below the hard minimum, run an aggressive-but-safe cleanup pass for DDx-owned scratch prefixes (ddx-home-*, ddx-provider-shim-*, ddx-fixture-bin-*, stale claim-liveness tmp files) with a shorter pressure-only age threshold. If cleanup cannot restore hard minimum capacity, stop the worker with a clear resource_exhausted/operator_attention event rather than repeatedly claiming beads that cannot run.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_resources.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_cleanup_test.go or resource preflight tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not delete non-DDx-owned /tmp content. Do not weaken ordinary cleanup safety when no resource pressure exists. Do not hide resource_exhausted; if cleanup fails, the worker must stop or surface operator attention clearly. Do not change provider routing.

description:
Hand-curated sub-agent prompts have been outperforming ddx work / ddx try in this session. Two competing hypotheses for why:
H1: ddx execution machinery (the 9 fail-prone layers) is unreliable — failure is in the workers/server code.
H2: Bead authoring quality is insufficient — beads punt investigation; hand-curation papers over the gap.

Both are plausible. Determining the relative contribution requires a 3-path study, NOT the original 2-path proposal.

THREE PATHS

Path A: ddx try / ddx work with the bead's auto-prompt verbatim (current production path).
Path B: Sub-agent dispatched with the bead's auto-prompt verbatim (NOT hand-curated). Same prompt as A; different executor. Isolates ddx machinery from prompt quality.
Path C: Sub-agent dispatched with operator hand-curated prompt (file:line cites, named tests, explicit non-scope, etc.). Establishes the ceiling.

INTERPRETATION
- A vs B differ → ddx machinery is the failure (file follow-ups against the 9 layers).
- B vs C differ → bead authoring quality is the failure (already covered by bead-quality-audit + retrofit).
- A == B << C → both are real, with bead quality being the dominant gap.

METHOD
Pick 5 representative CLOSED beads as fixtures: one trivial fix, one refactor child, one test addition, one multi-file feature, one documentation update. For each fixture, run all 3 paths on a branch from the bead's base-rev (parent of the original work commit). Throwaway commits — the original work is already in main. We're measuring path properties, not producing mergeable code.

MEASUREMENTS
Per path per bead:
- Time-to-first-claim (A) / time-to-first-output (B,C)
- Time-to-merge-eligible-commit (whether or not we merge)
- Attempts (A) / iterations (B,C)
- Status outcomes: success / no_changes / preserved / blocked / errored
- Cost: tokens, USD
- Manual interventions
- Failure mode classified per the 9-layer machinery list

OUTPUT
.ddx/executions/<run-id>/ddx-vs-subagent-comparison-2026-05-03.md with:
- Per-bead per-path table
- Aggregate stats (median + p99)
- Failure-mode distribution
- Hypothesis verdict (H1 vs H2 vs both)
- Recommendations for which path is appropriate for which bead-shape

TIMING
This study runs AFTER the executeloop refactor (C0-C13) lands so the ddx machinery is its post-refactor shape. Running pre-refactor measures behavior we're about to change. RELIABILITY-PRINCIPLES + bead-quality-audit + retrofit + refactor must all complete first. This bead is filed now and EXECUTION DEFERRED.

NOT IN SCOPE
- Fixing whatever the study reveals (separate bug beads filed from the study's findings)
- Running against pre-refactor ddx machinery (data we won't act on)
- Comparing different sub-agent harnesses (different concern)

EVIDENCE
- ddx-f339c399 documents the 2026-05-04 ddx try ddx-29058e2a --harness=codex no_changes outcome and is partial Path B-vs-C data favoring the bead-quality hypothesis.

description:
PROBLEM
On 2026-06-29 DDx recorded four unrelated provider subprocess failures only as transport: exit status 1, then immediately claimed another bead after each failure. That erased whether the child was killed by SIGKILL/SIGTERM and allowed a clustered infrastructure failure to consume multiple beads and model contexts without a recovery interval.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/executor.go:301-330 records only an integer ExitCode and discards exec.ExitError.ProcessState/syscall.WaitStatus signal evidence. cli/internal/agent/runner.go:351-390 copies only that exit code and stderr into Result. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:6036-6098 then collapses transport-like text into the generic transport outcome. The watch loop maintains no rolling timestamps for transport outcomes, so three failures inside ten minutes do not delay the next claim.

PROPOSED FIX
Carry portable termination metadata from OSExecutor through Result and ExecuteBeadReport, including a signal name/number when ProcessState proves a signal termination. Preserve ordinary nonzero-exit behavior. In watch mode, track transport-class failure timestamps for the current worker; after three within ten minutes, emit a transport_cluster_cooldown observation and apply a context-cancellable delay of at least five minutes before another claim. Reset/expire the rolling window after successful work or elapsed window time.

NON-SCOPE
Do not infer OOM without kernel evidence, change queue ordering, mutate the failed bead to blocked/proposed, add host-load sampling, or change durable_audit commit flow. The cooldown is worker/infra pacing and must not become a per-bead retry-after.

PARENT

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-6a2ce3bd is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 1 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
DDx-owned temporary homes, provider shims, and helper scratch are created directly under raw os.TempDir(), so /tmp remains the choke point even when DDx has a configured execution/runtime temp root with available space. The 2026-07-08 incident had /tmp at 100% inode use while the configured execution worktree root under /Users/erik/Projects/.ddx-exec-wt still had capacity.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:91 creates provider shims with os.MkdirTemp("", "ddx-provider-shim-").
cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:29 and runner_test.go:56 create ddx-home-* with os.MkdirTemp("", "ddx-home-"); equivalent command tests create the same prefix in cli/cmd/work_resource_exhausted_test.go:80, cli/cmd/try_test.go:823, and cli/cmd/doctor_test.go:85.

These producers bypass config.ExecutionScratchRoot / config.ExecutionWorktreeRoot and strand inode-heavy scratch under /tmp.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a shared helper for DDx-owned scratch temp dirs that prefers config.ExecutionScratchRoot(projectRoot) or the configured execution/runtime root when a project root is available, and falls back to os.TempDir() only when no configured root exists. Migrate provider shims and DDx-owned temp homes/fixture bins to the helper where production/runtime context is available. Keep tests hermetic by setting the helper root explicitly in tests.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go
- cli/internal/config/execution_worktree_root.go or a new scratch-temp helper package
- relevant tests in cli/internal/agent and cli/cmd

NON-SCOPE
Do not move claim-liveness in this bead; ddx-3986b89a covers claim heartbeat root selection. Do not change git worktree placement. Do not store long-lived user config in execution scratch. Do not require a project root for all tests; fallback behavior must remain.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- TestDDXScratchTempDirUsesConfiguredExecutionRoot proves a DDx scratch temp helper creates ddx-home/provider-shim style directories under the configured execution/runtime root when configured.
- TestDDXScratchTempDirFallsBackToOSTempDirWithoutConfiguredRoot proves fallback behavior remains when no project/config root is available.

Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
Cold-start or no-reuse reusable workspace allocation outcomes need explicit zero time-saved and bytes-saved telemetry, but the execution observability path does not copy savings values into payloads. Without explicit zeros, downstream telemetry cannot distinguish no savings from missing fields and may infer reuse wins outside the cold-start contract.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares and cleans up reusable workspaces without copying savings values into the execution event path for cold-start or no-reuse outcomes.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` has no cold-start savings fallback in the attempt path, so observability cannot emit zero-valued savings fields while preserving hit/miss behavior.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, parent `ddx-1436e204`, parent `ddx-5dda007b`, parent bead `ddx-54ff73df`, child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace hit and miss telemetry events", sibling child "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", sibling child "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", sibling child "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation", child "attempt-backend: calculate reusable workspace savings estimates from allocation outcomes", child "attempt-backend: emit zero reusable workspace savings for cold-start attempts", and child "attempt-backend: define reusable workspace savings telemetry fields". Ensure execution event / observability payloads emit zero time-saved and zero bytes-saved fields when the supplied reusable allocation outcome represents cold-start or no-reuse behavior. Preserve slot hit/miss counters and do not add reuse-win classification.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.
- Do not alter the estimate formula except as needed to consume the contract delivered by the savings-estimate child.
- Do not implement reuse-win classification; that belongs to the cold-start zero-savings child.

description:
PROBLEM
The cleanup-fixture split is not independently landable. Attempt 20260713T153145-d424151a correctly isolated TestWorkCleanup_RunsAfterSetupFailureBeforeNextClaim, added its outside-root sentinel regression, and passed the focused gate. The required full internal/agent gate still entered host-dependent fixture work and had to be interrupted after five minutes; the SIGQUIT snapshot was in TestWorkInterrupt_InFlightAttemptUnclaimsBead. Leaving the remaining production ExecutionCleanupManager fixtures for a dependent part 2 means part 1 cannot satisfy its own package acceptance before part 2 is allowed to run.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_cleanup_test.go:269-288 constructs a production NewExecutionCleanupManager without explicit TempRoot or ScratchRoots. The valid unlanded attempt patch shows this fixture needs roots below its own t.TempDir and an outside-root sentinel.
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_test.go:102-114 centralizes project-root setup but does not enforce hermetic effective cleanup roots across the many NewExecutionCleanupManager call sites in internal/agent tests.
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:830-843 derives the configured cache parent and os.TempDir whenever ScratchRoots is unset, so any missed test fixture can enumerate accumulated host state.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_test.go:3014-3027 creates stores through the normal config loader. In the failed full-suite snapshot, cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_disruption_test.go:250-279 was blocked under that helper while the test process remained host-dependent. This path must be audited along with cleanup runners so the package gate has no hidden global-root dependency.

PROPOSED FIX
Make this the atomic fixture-hermeticity repair. Recreate the valid attempt-20260713T153145-d424151a work-loop change: configure fixture-local TempRoot and ScratchRoots and add TestWorkCleanup_RunsAfterSetupFailureBeforeNextClaim_DoesNotTouchSharedScratchRoot. Add or extend a shared cleanup-test helper that requires every internal/agent fixture invoking a production ExecutionCleanupManager.Cleanup to use roots beneath its own t.TempDir, and audit all such call sites. Add a regression for newExecuteLoopTestStore/runInterruptedWorkAttempt if it can inherit process-global DDx/config roots. The completed change must make the focused fixtures and the full internal/agent package gate independently green in one commit.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_cleanup_test.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_test.go and the nearest cleanup fixture helpers/call sites
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_process_test.go and execution_resources_test.go where production cleanup is invoked
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_test.go and execute_bead_loop_disruption_test.go only as needed to make the observed store/config fixture hermetic

NON-SCOPE
Do not change production cleanup behavior, retention policy, or deletion semantics. Do not add a package-wide TestMain sandbox, skip tests, weaken timeouts, or treat a killed/incomplete full-suite run as success. Do not rely on an uncommitted worktree or /tmp artifact; the valid part-1 behavior is fully stated above.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-e6abf4a6. Deps: none. Supersedes the execution scope of ddx-12a41acc; that bead retains the failed-attempt audit and waits on this atomic repair.

description:
PROBLEM
Runtime artifact validation must inspect current-revision Verification evidence without modifying fixture files. If the spechonesty analyzer mutates fixtures while checking Complete/Implemented rows, it becomes unsafe for pre-commit and violates the analyzer contract.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no read-only guard around runtime-artifact existence checks over parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
Add focused read-only test coverage for the runtime artifact validation path using fixture files. The test should run validation through the parsed Verification rows and runtime artifact resolver, collect diagnostics in memory, and assert that fixture file contents and metadata relevant to mutation detection are unchanged after validation.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change diagnostic content beyond what is required to exercise read-only validation. Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that. Do not add document-restamping coverage in this bead; that is covered by the sibling child.

DEPS: parent ddx-e743ce67; grandparent ddx-29449fa5; root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the runtime artifact target resolver child. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

ROOT CAUSE
  cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_conflict_recovery.go:118 defines RunConflictRecovery(ctx, ConflictRecoveryInput) ConflictRecoveryOutput — the C4 extraction already landed. The bead description still refers to the old inline branch. The caller site is cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:847-878 (loop branches on ShouldAttemptConflictRecovery, then calls RunConflictRecovery). The try.Attempt API (cli/internal/agent/try/attempt.go:67, func Attempt(ctx, store, beadID, AttemptOpts) (Outcome, error)) does not yet call RunConflictRecovery; conflict recovery remains loop-owned.

PROPOSED FIX
  - Migrate RunConflictRecovery invocation from execute_bead_loop.go:847-878 into try.Attempt (cli/internal/agent/try/attempt.go) so Attempt's return Outcome already encodes conflict-recovery disposition.
  - Add try/conflict_recovery.go: thin adapter from ConflictRecoveryOutput to Outcome (Disposition=Merged → OutcomeSuccess, Park/NeedsHuman → OutcomePark).
  - Loop caller (execute_bead_loop.go:847) delegates to try.Attempt instead of calling RunConflictRecovery directly; removes the inline branch.
  - Add TestAttempt_ConflictRecovered_ReturnsMergedOutcome and TestAttempt_ConflictUnresolvable_ReturnsPark to cli/internal/agent/try/attempt_test.go.

NON-SCOPE
  - Deleting the attempted/hookFailed maps (C7, ddx-06eb05d8).
  - Heartbeat extraction (C11, ddx-0b8780db).
  - File renames (C13, ddx-387a0178).

INTERSECTIONS
- P1: fail-open at the layer boundary when conflict recovery is not applicable or cannot complete cleanly.
- P2: conflict recovery owns only its own conditions; the loop should delegate rather than infer recovery policy.
- P3: the worker panel should surface conflict-recovery transitions and any degraded path.
- P4: a bad bead X must not spill into bead Y; conflict recovery stays per-bead.

PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-43b6b5fe is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 4 of 4 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
The two principles of epic ddx-602ae31a (ddx home resolution + skills/personas install topology) must behave identically across both modes (in-tree and convention). Today there is no single test suite that drives the same scenarios through both modes; coverage is per-mode-ad-hoc and divergence between modes is invisible until operators hit it in production.

ROOT CAUSE
The two parent beads (ddx-06cbaa90 and ddx-937de9fc) each carry per-feature tests. Neither owns the cross-mode equivalence guarantee.

PROPOSED FIX

1. Add cli/internal/agent/test_mode_matrix_test.go (or equivalent suite under a new package) that parameterizes every behaviour-equivalence scenario across both modes:

  for mode in [Convention, InTree]:
    setup_fixture(mode)
    for scenario in [
      "bead-lifecycle":           create/show/update/close
      "bead-execution":           ddx try a bead, observe attempt evidence and state mutation
      "plugin-skill-resolution":  ddx-side plugin lookup honors precedence; agent-tier symlinks resolve to plugin content
      "persona-binding":          role → persona resolves correctly per binding config
      "worker-drain":             ddx work --watch picks beads and lands them
      "meta-prompt-sync":         CLAUDE.md (or equivalent) gets the right content
      "auto-commit-routing":      bead create/update auto-commit lands in the right git repo (project's vs XDG's)
      "attachments":              per-attempt event files written to the right anchor
      "index-lock-recovery":      gitlock recovery fires correctly in both modes
    ]:
      run scenario in current mode
      assert behaviour identical to the other mode modulo storage path

2. Fixture setup must be deterministic and isolated:
   - Convention mode fixture: tempdir as project root, no .ddx/; XDG_DATA_HOME pointed at a per-test tempdir; git remote set to a deterministic URL.
   - In-tree mode fixture: tempdir as project root WITH .ddx/ pre-created; XDG_DATA_HOME pointed elsewhere (must not be consulted).
   - Two clones of the same project share an XDG dir — explicitly tested as a separate sub-scenario.

3. Document the test-mode invariant in cli/internal/agent/test_mode_matrix_test.go's package doc: "Any behavior that diverges between Convention and InTree modes (other than the on-disk anchor) is a regression."

acceptance:
1. `TestReusableAttemptWorkspacePreservesOnlyAllowlistedSlotState` proves allocator-owned allowlisted metadata can survive while non-allowlisted files are removed.
2. `TestReusableAttemptWorkspaceFailsIntegrityCheckWhenScrubIncomplete` proves an incomplete reset or remaining disallowed residue prevents reuse.
3. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run 'Test(ReusableAttemptWorkspacePreservesOnlyAllowlistedSlotState|ReusableAttemptWorkspaceFailsIntegrityCheckWhenScrubIncomplete)' -count=1` passes.
4. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/config/...` passes.
5. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes on the final staged tree.
description:
PROBLEM
Reusable workspace scrubbing is not safe unless DDx preserves only allocator-owned slot state and refuses reuse whenever any disallowed residue remains after cleanup.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:116-149` and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:199-233` allocate fresh directories, so no integrity gate currently validates that a reused directory is clean at the requested base revision.
- Because cleanup deletes directories in `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:182-190` and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:252-259`, no code currently defines or verifies an explicit allowlist of reusable slot metadata that may survive between beads.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1019-1031` writes cleanup metadata that must not be accidentally treated as allowable allocator state.

PROPOSED FIX
Extend the shared scrub routine with an explicit allowlist and post-scrub integrity check. The allowlist must preserve only allocator-owned metadata required to identify or manage the reusable slot. Any non-allowlisted file, dirty index entry, modified tracked file, untracked source file, execution evidence, cleanup metadata, or environment-derived credential residue must cause reuse to fail rather than silently handing the workspace to the next bead.

GOVERNING ARTIFACTS
Parent bead: `ddx-388ca2af`. Parent container: `ddx-bb1410e1`. Depends on sibling allocator/config child: `attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface`.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this child concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not implement Rust/Cargo build-cache preservation or toolchain/lockfile invalidation.
- Do not change `execute_bead.go` orchestration or add telemetry.
- Do not implement backend-specific slot acquisition beyond enforcing the shared scrub routine's allowlist and integrity contract.

  The execute-bead subsystem files use execute_bead_* naming that conflates the orchestrator, the attempt, the review, and the loop under one prefix, making package boundaries and import graphs ambiguous. The refactor proposal was stored at /tmp/ and is unreadable post-session.

ROOT CAUSE
  cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go (drain loop), cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go (attempt), cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_orchestrator.go (land coordinator), cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go (landing), cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go (review), cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review_triage.go (review triage), cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go (disposition), and cli/internal/agent/executions_mirror.go (mirror) all share a flat package with unrelated concerns. The ddx try CLI command named in FEAT-010 does not exist (cli/cmd/try.go absent).

PROPOSED FIX
  Rename per the following table (no behavior change):
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go             -> cli/internal/agent/try/attempt.go (already exists; merge or verify)
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_orchestrator.go -> cli/internal/agent/try/land.go
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go         -> cli/internal/agent/try/coordinator.go
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go       -> cli/internal/agent/try/review.go
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review_triage.go -> cli/internal/agent/try/review_triage.go
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_status.go       -> cli/internal/agent/try/disposition.go
    cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go         -> cli/internal/agent/work/drain.go
    cli/internal/agent/executions_mirror.go         -> cli/internal/agent/try/mirror.go

  Rename identifiers: ExecuteBeadWorker -> work.Worker, ExecuteBeadWorker.Run -> work.Worker.Drain, ExecuteBead -> try.Attempt (FEAT-006 + FEAT-010).

  Add cli/cmd/try.go with cobra command "ddx try <bead-id>" invoking try.Attempt directly (FEAT-010 surface).

  Update FEAT-006 and FEAT-010 spec docs to reflect new package paths. Keep ExecuteBead* shims as typedefs; deletion is C14.

NON-SCOPE
  - Behavior changes to the drain loop or attempt logic.
  - Deletion of ExecuteBead* typedefs (C14).
  - ddx-dc157075 file-path reference migration if that bead has not yet landed.

INTERSECTIONS
- P2: file and identifier names should reflect the subsystem boundary and keep responsibilities separated.
- P5: ddx try as a first-class CLI surface makes the worker/attempt state easier for operators to see.
- P7: the refactor aligns names and prompt surface with the bead-as-prompt contract.

1. `TestLocalCloneAttemptBackendReusesWorkerSlotAcrossSequentialAttempts` runs two sequential attempts and proves the second receives the same healthy slot while checking out its requested base revision.
2. `TestReusableAttemptWorkspaceScrubsCrossBeadState` proves staged changes, modified tracked files, untracked files, evidence, environment-derived credentials, and attempt metadata from bead A are absent from bead B.
3. `TestReusableAttemptWorkspaceIsolatesConcurrentWorkers` proves concurrent attempts receive distinct workspace and build-cache paths and cannot observe or lock each other's mutable target state.
4. `TestReusableRustWorkspacePreservesCargoTargetAcrossBeads` uses a small Rust fixture or compiler wrapper to prove an unchanged dependency is not rebuilt on the second sequential attempt while source and base-revision correctness are preserved.
5. `TestReusableAttemptWorkspaceInvalidatesOnToolchainOrLockChange` proves Rust toolchain and dependency-lock incompatibilities trigger a safe cache invalidation without leaking workspace state.

8. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/config/... -run 'Test(LocalCloneAttemptBackendReusesWorkerSlotAcrossSequentialAttempts|ReusableAttemptWorkspaceScrubsCrossBeadState|ReusableAttemptWorkspaceIsolatesConcurrentWorkers|ReusableRustWorkspacePreservesCargoTargetAcrossBeads|ReusableAttemptWorkspaceInvalidatesOnToolchainOrLockChange|ReusableAttemptWorkspaceQuarantinesDirtyOrLiveSlot)' -count=1` passes.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx creates and deletes a fresh checkout for every bead attempt, discarding useful local build state. On Rust queues this causes every worker to rebuild large dependency graphs in separate per-attempt targets. In the live Niflheim queue, otherwise bounded documentation and code beads repeatedly spent roughly 20-24 minutes in cold `lefthook`/clippy runs while concurrent workers rebuilt jemalloc, aws-lc, and rdkafka and contended on Cargo locks. The isolation mechanism is amplifying CPU, disk I/O, storage, and wall-clock cost instead of sustaining queue throughput.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` selects `local-clone` as the default attempt backend.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:116-149` creates a linked worktree at a new attempt-specific path, and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:182-190` removes it during cleanup.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:199-233` creates a new local clone for every attempt, and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:252-259` deletes that clone during cleanup.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:567-571` and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:556-558` include the attempt ID in workspace paths, preventing sequential reuse.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:568-577` preserves a shared Go cache only for Docker; linked-worktree and local-clone attempts have no equivalent reusable build state.
- `cli/internal/config/types.go:348-364` exposes backend and temporary-root configuration but no reusable workspace-slot or language build-cache policy.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares a new workspace for every attempt and defers destructive cleanup afterward.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a bounded pool of reusable isolated workspace slots keyed by project, backend, worker slot, and trust boundary. Sequential attempts may reuse a slot after DDx resets tracked state to the requested base revision and scrubs staged, modified, untracked, evidence, credential, and process state. Preserve only explicitly allowlisted build state, including a per-slot Cargo target directory and package caches. Concurrent workers must receive distinct slots and must never mutate the same Cargo target. Invalidate or quarantine a slot after cleanup failure, live descendants, repository identity mismatch, toolchain/lockfile incompatibility, or failed integrity checks. Add age and disk high-water eviction, an opt-out/configuration surface, and hit/miss plus time/bytes-saved telemetry. Apply the allocator to both linked-worktree and local-clone backends; cleanup should return a healthy slot to the pool instead of always deleting it.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.

description:
PROBLEM
Docker-clone attempts currently make DDx responsible for installing concrete Claude, Codex, and Gemini binaries, copying their private credentials and settings, selecting provider environment-variable prefixes, and seeding provider-specific Fizeau quota caches. This duplicates Fizeau runtime knowledge and becomes stale whenever Fizeau adds or changes a harness.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:263-280 prepares a DDx-owned synthetic home for the embedded runtime.
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:290-347 constructs the container invocation and calls dockerToolMounts before dispatch.
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:803-871 applies DDx-owned tool mounts and credential environment forwarding.
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:902-914 hard-codes claude, codex, and gemini binary discovery.
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:941-975 copies Codex and Claude credentials/settings plus Claude, Codex, and Gemini Fizeau quota snapshots.
- cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:1002-1020 hard-codes Anthropic, Codex, Fizeau, Gemini, Google, OpenAI, and OpenRouter environment prefixes.
- Fizeau bead fizeau-725d478d owns the missing public portable-runtime materialization seam; fizeau-b9a2037c must publish that seam in the pinned module before DDx consumes it.

PROPOSED FIX
Pin the released Fizeau version containing PreparePortableRuntime or its final public equivalent. During Docker workspace preparation, ask Fizeau to materialize one complete route-neutral runtime bundle under the attempt runtime root. Store only the returned opaque generic mount/environment/cleanup plan. Apply returned mounts and environment names byte-for-byte without inspecting, filtering, naming, or selecting a harness/provider/model. Invoke bundle cleanup during normal cleanup and failed preparation. Delete dockerToolMounts, provider-specific home copies, provider environment prefixes, and all concrete harness/credential/quota strings from the Docker backend. Retain DDx-owned container identity, worktree mount, prompt path, DDX correlation variables, resource limits, project caches, network selection, candidate transport, and DDx container cleanup.

NON-SCOPE
Do not design or duplicate the portable-runtime contract in DDx, choose a concrete route from bundle contents, make Fizeau own DDx worktrees/container resource policy/verification/landing/tracker state, remove provider-process supervision or text classification before separately pinned v0.15 guarantees, bake credentials into images, or emit secrets in evidence.

description:
PROBLEM
`ddx doctor` still reports DDx package-layer topology instead of checking whether required marketplace skills/plugins are available. Current code at `cli/cmd/doctor.go:292-298` prints `Checking Skill Install Topology` and calls `reportSkillInstallTopology`; `cli/cmd/doctor.go:432-462` reports `Global Install` and `Project Install` for `.ddx/plugins/ddx`. The new product requirement is for doctor to check configured plugin marketplace skill availability for `ddx`, `helix`, and `easel-skills`, and suggest installing missing ones.

ROOT CAUSE
Doctor is coupled to the old DDx package install model. It has no loader for marketplace requirements from the ddx-library package config and no deterministic availability checker for marketplace-installed skills.

PROPOSED FIX
- Replace the Skill Install Topology section in `cli/cmd/doctor.go:292-298` with a `Plugin Marketplace Skills` check.
- Load required marketplace plugin requirements from the active ddx library package config added by dependency bead `ddx-7abf3a7a`. Resolve package config from project/global/baked-in DDx package layers, but use those layers only to find config, not as the success signal for skill availability.
- Implement deterministic availability checks from the configured hints, for example scanning explicit skill directories and/or plugin metadata paths declared in config. The exact sources must be documented in the code and tests; do not shell out to `npx` during doctor.
- When config is unreadable or absent, use a small baked-in fallback containing `ddx`, `helix`, and `easel-skills`, and print that fallback requirements are being used so stale config is visible.
- Missing marketplace skills/plugins should be warning-level and exit 0; a broken legacy symlink may remain fatal only if the existing legacy-symlink guard still detects harmful project-local state.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not install marketplace plugins from doctor. Print install commands only.
- Do not hardcode the normal requirement list in doctor when package config is readable.
- Do not remove `ddx install` command registration in this bead; sibling bead `cli: remove top-level ddx install commands` owns that.

DEPS
Depends on ddx-7abf3a7a for typed package config.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-8a78ee90 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 3 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Execute-bead agents are instructed to run `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then run `git commit`. The repository-installed Git pre-commit hook invokes Lefthook again on the same staged tree. During attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4`, a small containment patch ran the full staged `./cmd` plus `./internal/agent` race gate twice explicitly after one test correction, then `git commit` launched a third full pass on the identical final staged tree. The second explicit pass alone spent more than 18 minutes in `go test` output processing. This duplicate gate contract serializes the queue without adding evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2104-2113` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2137-2148` require rich and embedded agents to rerun `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then commit exactly once, without recognizing that the implementation commit invokes the installed hook.
- `lefthook.yml:205-216` maps staged Go files to package-wide race tests, so each duplicate invocation can repeat multi-minute `./cmd` and `./internal/agent` gates.
- `.git/hooks/pre-commit:11-18` invokes Lefthook for ordinary `git commit`, making a separately requested manual invocation redundant when the staged tree is unchanged.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the ordinary implementation commit hook the single authoritative staged pre-commit gate. Update both execute-bead prompt variants and integrity evidence so agents stage the exact commit set, run `git commit` normally, and treat the hook output/exit status from that commit as satisfying the bead’s `lefthook run pre-commit` acceptance criterion. If a workflow explicitly runs the hook before commit, reuse that success only when a content/config fingerprint proves the staged tree and hook inputs are identical; otherwise rerun. A failed hook must abort the commit and remain a failed gate.

NON-SCOPE
Using `--no-verify`, setting `LEFTHOOK=0`, weakening or removing repository hooks, reusing evidence after any staged-tree or hook-config change, caching across attempts, bypassing human commits, or changing which tests the hook selects.

PARENT
None; root worker-throughput regression observed while draining the Niflheim queue.

DEPS
Related to `ddx-2afca9c9` (test-output/runtime headroom) and `ddx-03568f89` (gate evidence); no implementation dependency.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run "^(TestExecuteBeadPrompt_UsesImplementationCommitAsSinglePreCommitGate|TestExecuteBeadImplementationCommit_RunsPreCommitOnceForUnchangedIndex|TestExecuteBeadImplementationCommit_HookFailureAbortsCommit|TestExecuteBeadPreCommitEvidence_InvalidatedByStagedMutation)$" -count=1 -timeout 120s` passes.
- `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s` passes.
- `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-53df5e2f is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 2 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
# PROBLEM
The legacy `*Store.MigrateToAxon` method (now exposed via `Migrator.MigrateToAxon` in MIG bead, returning `ErrDeprecated`) writes JSONL files under `.ddx/axon/` rather than performing an actual JSONL→Postgres migration. Per the audit in `docs/plans/plan-2026-05-10-axon-only-architecture.md`, production AxonStore deployment requires migrating existing `.ddx/beads.jsonl` corpora into Lakebase Postgres. The real importer is unimplemented.

# ROOT CAUSE
`cli/internal/bead/migrate.go` (function previously at `*Store.MigrateToAxon`, now folded into `*storeMigrator` per MIG bead) writes JSONL into a sidecar directory. The function does not connect to Postgres or invoke `AxonStore.Apply`/`AxonStore.Create`. Production deployment cannot use it to populate Lakebase.

# PROPOSED FIX

1. Implement a real importer in `cli/internal/bead/internal/storage/import_postgres.go` (or equivalent post-BL location). The importer:
   - Reads `.ddx/beads.jsonl` (and `.ddx/beads-archive.jsonl` if present) — uses existing JSONL parser.
   - For each bead, calls `axonStore.Create(ctx, &b)` to insert into Postgres. Idempotent on `ErrConflict` (skip + log).
   - For each bead, appends events via `axonStore.Apply(ctx, id, AppendEventOp{...})` per TD-027 §13 vocabulary (events come from `Extra["events"]` on the JSONL bead or from sidecar `.ddx/attachments/<bead>/events.jsonl`).
   - Tracks progress, supports `--dry-run` (counts without writes), `--limit N` (batched migration).
   - Verifies post-migration: read back beads from Postgres, assert field-for-field equality with source JSONL (sample-based for large corpora).

2. Expose via `Migrator` interface (added in MIG): rename/replace `MigrateToAxon` with the real implementation; same method name, different (correct) behavior.

3. Update `cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go` to support the importer with appropriate flags:
   - `ddx bead migrate --to-axon --dry-run`
   - `ddx bead migrate --to-axon --apply [--limit N]`
   - `ddx bead migrate --to-axon --verify` (read-back + checksum)

4. Remove the deprecated JSONL-writing behavior. `ErrDeprecated` return from MIG bead is replaced by the real implementation.

# NON-SCOPE
- Schema-versioning migration ladder (separate concern; deferred until first v1→v2 breaking change).
- Real-wire integration test against actual Postgres — separate WIRE bead.
- Continuous sync between JSONL and Postg

Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- Implement the remaining bounded slice of the parent bead.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
Slot-backed preparation can create reusable workspaces, but execute-bead cleanup still follows the disposable-workspace model. A successful attempt can destructively delete a healthy reusable slot instead of returning it to the pool, and the cleanup path must not regress preservation or evidence behavior.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` installs a cleanup defer that ends in `_ = attemptBackend.Cleanup(ctx, workspace)`, so healthy workspaces are deleted after successful attempts rather than released for reuse.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1019-1031` writes per-attempt cleanup metadata into the workspace, so release must happen only after the sibling scrub/quarantine path has removed per-attempt state and decided whether the slot is healthy.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` also owns existing `runtime.PreserveAttemptWorktree`, `KeepOnError`, and evidence-preservation branches that must remain behaviorally unchanged.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, and the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". In `execute_bead.go`, replace the successful-attempt unconditional destructive cleanup branch with attempt-backend release semantics: after per-attempt metadata is written and scrub/quarantine has classified the workspace as healthy, return the reusable slot to the pool; if quarantine is required, delete/quarantine according to the sibling backend contract. Keep preservation branches short-circuiting before release/deletion as they do today.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.

description:
PROBLEM
The public DDx execution vocabulary is supposed to be `ddx run`, `ddx try`, and `ddx work`, but large parts of the codebase still use legacy `execute-bead` / `work` names in public help, comments, server worker kinds, GraphQL models, tests, docs, tracker metadata helpers, and internal symbols. Operators now see mixed terms and developers keep adding new code under the old names.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1485-1563 still defines the legacy `ddx agent work` cobra surface as if it were primary: help says "work is the primary queue-driven execution surface", examples use `ddx agent work`, and deprecation text still names work rather than pointing to `ddx work`.
- cli/cmd/agent_cmd.go:1590-1940 keeps the main work implementation named `runAgentExecuteLoopImpl`, `writeExecuteLoopResult`, and `ExecuteBeadLoopResult`, so new work-path changes naturally copy the old terminology.
- cli/cmd/try.go:213-333 implements the new `ddx try` command by constructing `ExecuteBeadExecutor`, `ExecuteBeadRuntime`, `ExecuteBeadWorker`, and `ExecuteBeadLoopRuntime`, so the new public command still routes through legacy names.
- cli/internal/server/graphql/models.go:2233-2281 and cli/internal/server/frontend/e2e/workers.spec.ts:343-397 expose worker kind/comment strings as `work` / `execute-bead`, which leaks legacy naming through API and UI fixtures.
- docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-031-bead-state-machine.md:215-262 still describes attempt results and retry metadata as `execute-bead` / `work-*`, even while FEAT-010 and ADR-023 name the lifecycle `try` / `work`.
- Existing related beads are partially stale or narrower than this repo-wide cleanup: ddx-387a0178 owns C13 file/identifier renames and still says `ddx try` does not exist, while ddx-29058e2a / ddx-1a9cc01f still propose `ExecuteLoopSpec` naming for a work-side spec.

WHY THE NAMES DIVERGED
The codebase grew from the historical `ddx agent execute-bead` and `ddx agent work` commands. FEAT-010 introduced the clearer layered vocabulary (`run` = invocation atom, `try` = one bead attempt, `work` = queue drain), and `ddx try` / `ddx work` now exist as the intended operator surface. The implementation retained old symbols and compatibility aliases, so old names persisted as the easiest local pattern to copy.

PROPOSED FIX
- Perform a repo-wide terminology audit using `rg -n "work|ExecuteLoop|execute loop|execute-bead|ExecuteBead|execute bead"` and classify each hit as: public/user-facing rename, internal compatibility alias to retain, durable metadata key to retain with documentation, historical docs intentionally retained, or generated fixture/test data.

- Rename non-compatibility internal types/functions introduced by the FEAT-010 path from ExecuteLoop/ExecuteBead vocabulary to Work/Try vocabulary. Coordinate with ddx-387a0178 C13; if C13 already performs a rename, fold this cleanup into or after it rather than duplicating work.

- Re-scope or update related open beads whose titles/descriptions still establish new `ExecuteLoop*` names (notably ddx-29058e2a and ddx-1a9cc01f) so future work does not add fresh legacy terminology.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not remove the legacy `ddx agent work` or `ddx agent execute-bead` command aliases in this bead; they are compatibility surfaces unless a governing doc explicitly authorizes removal.
- Do not rename durable tracker keys or historical event kinds if doing so would break existing `.ddx/beads.jsonl`, `.ddx/executions`, worker records, or archive reads. Document retained keys instead.
- Do not change work/try behavior, queue ordering, claim semantics, routing policy, or Fizeau integration.
- Do not hand-edit `.ddx/beads.jsonl`; update any related bead metadata only with `ddx bead update` / `ddx bead dep`.

- ddx-29058e2a and ddx-1a9cc01f: ExecuteLoopSpec naming conflicts with the intended WorkSpec/WorkRequest vocabulary; update or supersede as part of this cleanup.

description:

description:
PROBLEM
The two principles of epic ddx-602ae31a (ddx home resolution + skills/personas install topology) must behave identically across both modes (in-tree and convention). Today there is no single test suite that drives the same scenarios through both modes; coverage is per-mode-ad-hoc and divergence between modes is invisible until operators hit it in production.

ROOT CAUSE
The two parent beads (ddx-06cbaa90 and ddx-937de9fc) each carry per-feature tests. Neither owns the cross-mode equivalence guarantee.

PROPOSED FIX

1. Add cli/internal/agent/test_mode_matrix_test.go (or equivalent suite under a new package) that parameterizes every behaviour-equivalence scenario across both modes:

  for mode in [Convention, InTree]:
    setup_fixture(mode)
    for scenario in [
      "bead-lifecycle":           create/show/update/close
      "bead-execution":           ddx try a bead, observe attempt evidence and state mutation
      "plugin-skill-resolution":  ddx-side plugin lookup honors precedence; agent-tier symlinks resolve to plugin content
      "persona-binding":          role → persona resolves correctly per binding config
      "worker-drain":             ddx work --watch picks beads and lands them
      "meta-prompt-sync":         CLAUDE.md (or equivalent) gets the right content
      "auto-commit-routing":      bead create/update auto-commit lands in the right git repo (project's vs XDG's)
      "attachments":              per-attempt event files written to the right anchor
      "index-lock-recovery":      gitlock recovery fires correctly in both modes
    ]:
      run scenario in current mode
      assert behaviour identical to the other mode modulo storage path

2. Fixture setup must be deterministic and isolated:
   - Convention mode fixture: tempdir as project root, no .ddx/; XDG_DATA_HOME pointed at a per-test tempdir; git remote set to a deterministic URL.
   - In-tree mode fixture: tempdir as project root WITH .ddx/ pre-created; XDG_DATA_HOME pointed elsewhere (must not be consulted).
   - Two clones of the same project share an XDG dir — explicitly tested as a separate sub-scenario.

3. Document the test-mode invariant in cli/internal/agent/test_mode_matrix_test.go's package doc: "Any behavior that diverges between Convention and InTree modes (other than the on-disk anchor) is a regression."

4. SPEC UPDATES — propagate the resolver/mode model to every doc that references .ddx/ paths or project state. Each spec update added in this bead's commit cites principle-numbered tags so future readers see the link:
   - TD-031 bead state machine — "Storage anchors via ddxroot.Path(); see ddx-06cbaa90."
   - SD-019 multi-project-server-topology — Project identity from `host/owner/repo`; reference ddx-06cbaa90.
   - SD-020 multi-machine-coordinator-topology — same.
   - ADR-021 operator-prompt-beads-web-write-path — reference ddx-06cbaa90.
   - workers-sessions-operator-surface.md — worker status paths through ddxroot.Path().
   - plan-2026-04-29-artifact-and-run-architecture — FEAT-010 paths through resolver.
   - library/skills/ddx/SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md — install precedence per ddx-937de9fc.
   - library/README.md — install topology overview.

NON-SCOPE
- New behaviours (every scenario in the matrix is already covered by ddx-06cbaa90 or ddx-937de9fc per-feature tests; this is the cross-mode equivalence layer).
- Migration tooling for existing in-tree repos (out of scope; this repo stays in-tree).

DEPS
ddx-06cbaa90 (ddx home resolution).
ddx-937de9fc (skills/personas/plugins).

description:
PROBLEM
While `ddx work` executes a Codex bead, its pre-commit or package tests can legitimately launch another provider CLI as a fixture. The running-phase provider guard currently treats every differently named provider anywhere below the worker as a leaked non-route process and terminates it. On 2026-07-13, attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4` ran `go test -short -race ./internal/agent` under Codex and the guard terminated ten short-lived Claude descendants with reason `running_phase_non_route_provider_child`, allowing queue supervision to perturb its own verification.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_children_unix.go:18-58` discovers the full worker descendant tree but flattens each provider candidate into a `providerChildProcess` without retaining PPID or ancestry ownership.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_children.go:180-211` terminates every provider candidate whose provider name differs from the active route, even when that candidate is a descendant of the active implementation harness rather than a direct or sibling discovery leak.

PROPOSED FIX
Retain enough ancestry information to distinguish provider CLIs launched underneath the active route harness from provider CLIs launched directly by worker lifecycle/model-discovery paths. Preserve active-harness descendants during the running phase, continue terminating direct or sibling non-route leaks, and record the ownership disposition in status/evidence so operators can audit why a process was preserved or reaped.

NON-SCOPE
Disabling the running guard, preserving arbitrary direct worker children, weakening attempt-end cleanup after the implementation harness exits, changing provider routing, or ignoring genuine model-discovery leaks.

PARENT
`ddx-f84ee9a7` (Niflheim provider-test CPU incident).

DEPS
Related to `ddx-93d8b7c8`; no implementation dependency.

description:
PROBLEM
Attempt 20260713T145533-c006900a for ddx-8a78ee90 ran for 32m43s with a populated Codex route, repeatedly executing a known-doomed 600-second package suite. The documented 30-minute running-phase watchdog did not fire because route activity kept the attempt classified as healthy. Operator intervention was required to release the lease and stop CPU/I/O consumption.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3524-3539 installs only the phase-empty progress watchdog for the attempt lifetime.
- cli/internal/agent/work/watchdog.go:49-80 resets the phase-empty timer whenever harness, model, or route is populated, so a routed model can stay active indefinitely while making no useful progress.
- cli/internal/agent/types.go:415-421 gives the provider a separate three-hour absolute wall-clock cap, which is too broad to serve as a queue-attempt lease budget.
- cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:32-39 kills only the original provider process group; ddx-7df6b12a owns the attempt controller required to include descendants that call setsid or reparent.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a work/try active-attempt wall-clock budget with a 30-minute default, an explicit operator override for legitimate longer work, and an explicit zero value to disable only when requested. Run it beside the existing phase-empty watchdog. On expiry, cancel the attempt, release its lease, append operator_attention with bead ID, attempt ID, elapsed time, configured budget, and last activity, and continue draining. Terminate all attempt-controller members through the controller introduced by ddx-7df6b12a so session-changing and reparented tool children cannot survive. Use the same default and override semantics for manual/offline and server-managed workers.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go and cli/internal/agent/work watchdog helpers/tests
- cli/cmd/work.go and cli/cmd/try.go for shared flag/config plumbing
- attempt-controller integration points introduced by ddx-7df6b12a
- operator-attention rendering/tests for the new timeout reason

NON-SCOPE
Do not shorten the generic ddx run three-hour provider cap. Do not change queue ordering, provider routing, the phase-empty watchdog, or long-running bead acceptance commands. Do not rely on process ancestry alone.

PARENT AND DEPS
Root reliability incident. Depends on ddx-7df6b12a for attempt-controller membership and cleanup.

description:
PROBLEM
Cold-start attempts must appear in the same combined reusable workspace telemetry event shape as reused attempts, with explicit zero time-saved and bytes-saved values. Without this, operators cannot compare reuse wins against cold starts from one event stream.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` creates and cleans up cold-start workspaces but does not emit a combined reusable workspace telemetry record for that path.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` exposes backend outcome metadata, but the cold-start path does not consistently translate miss outcomes into explicit zero savings in the combined telemetry record.

- A canonical Bead data model (field enumeration + invariants + JSONL wire format + schema-versioning policy)

description:
PROBLEM
The server documents resolver rebuilds the full artifact graph on every page request, even when the underlying graph has not changed. On a 2000-artifact corpus, this produces visible latency on every load and makes concurrent requests redundantly expensive.

ROOT CAUSE
- cli/internal/server/graphql_resolver.go (or equivalent resolver file): the documents resolver calls the full graph-build pipeline on every GraphQL request without checking if the graph revision has changed since the last build.
- No normalized artifact cache (by graph revision) exists — every request starts cold.
- The search path in the documents resolver also rebuilds the full artifact list on every search call.
- ddx-5681cc57 (2k fixture) is a dep: cache design must be validated against the 2k scale fixture.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a cache keyed by graph revision (mtime-based, as recommended in the perf epic): store normalized artifact list (lowercased title/path/id/mediaType) keyed by revision string.
- Add search to documents resolver: filter the cached normalized list by search query.
- Add invalidation on file change: detect mtime changes and invalidate cache entry.
- Ensure concurrent requests don't double-build (single-flight pattern or sync.Once per revision).

NON-SCOPE
- Caching for resolvers other than documents.
- CI performance gate (that is a later bead).

cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_stay_alive_test.go:1244-1286 deliberately sets core.bare=true in a script-harness fixture, and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_env_isolation_test.go:181-237 asserts a separate contamination case does not affect the primary checkout. The observed full-hook run of `go test -short -race ./internal/agent` nevertheless rewrote /home/erik/Projects/ddx/.git/config at 2026-07-17 09:41 with core.bare=true and test user values. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_git_isolation.go:20-55 enables worktree config and seeds per-worktree config, while its wrapper at lines 169-229 only intercepts commands executed through the agent harness. Test fixtures and subprocesses can still select the shared config, so the test suite can corrupt the checkout it is supposed to isolate.

PROPOSED FIX
Make every fixture and helper that mutates Git configuration operate only on a dedicated temporary repository/config scope, never the caller checkout or its shared common gitdir. Audit runGitInteg/newScriptHarnessRepo and execute-bead isolation setup for inherited GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, and common-config selection. Add a deterministic regression that runs the exact affected agent test path from a real linked worktree of a primary repository, snapshots primary .git/config and config.worktree before and after, and proves core.bare, core.worktree, user.name, and user.email remain byte-identical while the fixture still proves the intended repair/isolation behavior. Fail closed if a fixture cannot establish a private config scope.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken the existing core.bare/core.worktree repair behavior, remove execute-bead config isolation, alter user project Git configuration, or change DDx/Fizeau routing. This bead owns test and execution-isolation correctness only; stale index-lock recovery is ddx-3f156500 and main-git lock safety is ddx-1c8d9319.

PARENT

No deps. This is an independent test-isolation defect discovered while validating ddx-3f156500.

description:

Parent bead ddx-359e812b is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 1 of 3 of that parent scope.

`ddx-359e812b` is still too broad for the remaining gap. `docs/helix/03-test/test-plans/TP-002-server-web-ui.md:340-351,353-363` already splits the planned work into TC-018.4 and TC-019.4, while the existing Playwright coverage in `cli/internal/server/frontend/e2e/beads-queue-mutations.spec.ts:210-268` and `cli/internal/server/frontend/e2e/spec-editing.spec.ts:204-256` already covers the mocked forwarded paths. `cli/internal/server/frontend/e2e/federation-2node.spec.ts:219-307` already covers the read-federation shell around the owner-write entry points.

ROOT CAUSE
FEAT-026 routes `beadCreate`, `beadUpdate`, `beadApprove`, `beadBlock`, `beadCancel`, `beadReopen`, and `documentWrite` only to the owner node and never broadcasts (`docs/helix/01-frame/features/FEAT-026-federation.md:22-29,160-177`). The stale bead mixed that live owner-targeted write persistence work with already-covered UI smoke and the separate ts-net guard.

PROPOSED FIX
- Track only the live owner-targeted write persistence gap: bead create/edit and `documentWrite` forwarding, offline-spoke refusal, and idempotent request IDs.
- Keep the ts-net guard as a separate bead if it still needs work.
- Guard the narrowed scope with `TestFederatedBeadWrite_ForwardsToOwner`, `TestFederatedDocumentWrite_ForwardsToOwner`, `TestFederatedWrite_RejectsOfflineSpoke`, and `TestFederatedWrite_IdempotentRequestID`.
- Do not expand this bead back into federation read smoke or mocked Playwright smoke coverage.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not add new federation read smoke.
- Do not add screenshot assertions.
- Do not implement managed-node outbound control from ADR-028.
- Do not reintroduce the mocked Playwright smoke paths into this bead.

RECONCILIATION NOTES
- `TP-002-server-web-ui.md:340-351,353-363` isolates the bead and document write rows this bead is narrowing to.
- `beads-queue-mutations.spec.ts:210-268` already covers the mocked spoke bead-write forwarding smoke.
- `spec-editing.spec.ts:204-256` already covers the mocked spoke document-write forwarding smoke.
- `federation-2node.spec.ts:219-307` already covers the read-federation shell around the owner-write entry points.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `ddx bead show ddx-359e812b` is narrowed to live owner-targeted bead/document write persistence or is closed/superseded.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
Reusable workspace observability needs a single combined event containing slot hit/miss counts plus time-saved and bytes-saved values for both reuse and cold-start attempts. Without that combined event, operators must correlate separate signals and cannot reliably compare reuse wins against cold starts.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares and cleans up workspaces but does not emit one combined reusable workspace telemetry record with hit/miss counts and savings values.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` historically did not expose outcome metadata that lets telemetry report both allocation counts and savings estimates together.
- No attempt-path savings counters exist, so cold starts and reuse hits cannot be summarized in one event.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, parent `ddx-1436e204`, parent `ddx-5dda007b`, child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace hit and miss telemetry events", sibling child "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", sibling child "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", sibling child "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation", child "attempt-backend: calculate reusable workspace savings estimates from allocation outcomes", child "attempt-backend: emit zero reusable workspace savings for cold-start attempts", child "attempt-backend: carry reusable workspace savings through execution telemetry", and child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace savings for reused attempts". Emit or update the combined reusable workspace execution telemetry event so every attempt reports slot hit count, slot miss count, time-saved, and bytes-saved. Reused attempts should carry savings from the allocation outcome; cold-start attempts should carry explicit zero savings.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.
- Do not alter the estimate formula except as needed to consume the contract delivered by the savings-estimate child.
- Do not change the existing Docker attempt backend shared-cache behaviour while adding this event.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-53df5e2f requires ddx bead migrate --to-axon to call the Axon importer with correct dry-run, apply, limit, attachment-copy, and JSON stats options. This routing should be verified independently from help text, validation, verify mode, and storage fidelity.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The CLI reads migration flags at cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go:44 and routes --to-axon into Migrator.MigrateToAxon at cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go:55. The relevant flags are registered at cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go:202, and the stats shape returned by the importer is defined at cli/internal/bead/migrate.go:609. Without explicit dry-run and apply routing tests, operators can run --to-axon --dry-run or --to-axon --apply --limit N --json and receive output from a command that silently passed incorrect Migrator options.

PROPOSED FIX
Update cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go and cmd tests so --to-axon --dry-run --json calls Migrator.MigrateToAxon with DryRun true and no apply requirement, and --to-axon --apply --limit 7 --json passes Limit 7 and CopyAttachments true. Ensure JSON and human output expose bead, event, attachment, dry-run, and limit values from the migrator stats for these modes.

NON-SCOPE
- Schema-versioning migration ladder; deferred until first v1-to-v2 breaking change.
- Real-wire integration test against actual Postgres; separate WIRE bead.
- Continuous sync between JSONL and Postgres.
- Storage importer internals except as needed to satisfy the Migrator interface; sibling children own importer apply/fidelity behavior.
- New backend selection policy outside the existing Migrator/NewStore construction path.
- Do not claim or edit parent bead ddx-53df5e2f tracker data manually; tracker mutations must go through ddx bead commands.
- Help text, invalid flag-combination rejection, and verify mode are owned by sibling child beads.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
TD-027.

DEPENDENCY TO PRESERVE WHEN FILING
Parent dependency ID ddx-3d96c6f9.

description:
PROBLEM
When an implementation provider exits non-zero or otherwise fails after leaving a dirty worktree, execute-bead still synthesizes an implementation commit. The synthetic `git commit` runs the full repository pre-commit hook even though DDx already knows the attempt failed. Live attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4` first failed during the agent-owned commit hook, then DDx launched a second `chore: execute-bead iteration` commit and repeated the same multi-minute race hook against unsafe partial code. This wastes CPU, delays lease release, and risks turning a failed partial patch into commit-shaped evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1314-1377` gates synthesis only on unchanged HEAD plus a dirty worktree. It records `ExecuteBeadOutcomeTaskFailed` in the preliminary result when `exitCode != 0`, but proceeds to `SynthesizeCommit` anyway.
- `cli/internal/agent/gitops_real.go:148-179` implements `SynthesizeCommit` with ordinary `git commit`, so repository hooks run for this already-failed attempt. The synthesis error is not used to avoid the expensive call because failure classification happens later.

PROPOSED FIX
Classify a non-zero provider exit or provider execution error before dirty-worktree synthesis. For failed attempts, do not call `SynthesizeCommit` or any commit hook. Preserve the dirty implementation diff as a durable bundle-relative rescue patch, record its path in the result, and continue normal `task_failed` cleanup and retry handling. Keep synthesis unchanged for successful zero-exit dirty attempts that provide no no-changes rationale.

NON-SCOPE
Do not bypass hooks for successful implementation commits, automatically land or commit failed partial work, weaken successful-attempt verification, change retry limits, or fold the valid-rationale behavior owned by `ddx-232aa2c0` into this bead.

PARENT
None; root execute-bead failure-path regression observed during the Niflheim queue drain.

DEPS
None. Related to `ddx-232aa2c0` for rationale-before-synthesis ordering and `ddx-8a78ee90` for duplicate successful-path hook execution.

description:
# PROBLEM
The legacy `*Store.MigrateToAxon` method (now exposed via `Migrator.MigrateToAxon` in MIG bead, returning `ErrDeprecated`) writes JSONL files under `.ddx/axon/` rather than performing an actual JSONL→Postgres migration. Per the audit in `docs/plans/plan-2026-05-10-axon-only-architecture.md`, production AxonStore deployment requires migrating existing `.ddx/beads.jsonl` corpora into Lakebase Postgres. The real importer is unimplemented.

# ROOT CAUSE
`cli/internal/bead/migrate.go` (function previously at `*Store.MigrateToAxon`, now folded into `*storeMigrator` per MIG bead) writes JSONL into a sidecar directory. The function does not connect to Postgres or invoke `AxonStore.Apply`/`AxonStore.Create`. Production deployment cannot use it to populate Lakebase.

# PROPOSED FIX

1. Implement a real importer in `cli/internal/bead/internal/storage/import_postgres.go` (or equivalent post-BL location). The importer:
   - Reads `.ddx/beads.jsonl` (and `.ddx/beads-archive.jsonl` if present) — uses existing JSONL parser.
   - For each bead, calls `axonStore.Create(ctx, &b)` to insert into Postgres. Idempotent on `ErrConflict` (skip + log).
   - For each bead, appends events via `axonStore.Apply(ctx, id, AppendEventOp{...})` per TD-027 §13 vocabulary (events come from `Extra["events"]` on the JSONL bead or from sidecar `.ddx/attachments/<bead>/events.jsonl`).
   - Tracks progress, supports `--dry-run` (counts without writes), `--limit N` (batched migration).
   - Verifies post-migration: read back beads from Postgres, assert field-for-field equality with source JSONL (sample-based for large corpora).

2. Expose via `Migrator` interface (added in MIG): rename/replace `MigrateToAxon` with the real implementation; same method name, different (correct) behavior.

3. Update `cli/cmd/bead_migrate.go` to support the importer with appropriate flags:
   - `ddx bead migrate --to-axon --dry-run`
   - `ddx bead migrate --to-axon --apply [--limit N]`
   - `ddx bead migrate --to-axon --verify` (read-back + checksum)

4. Remove the deprecated JSONL-writing behavior. `ErrDeprecated` return from MIG bead is replaced by the real implementation.

# NON-SCOPE
- Schema-versioning migration ladder (separate concern; deferred until first v1→v2 breaking change).
- Real-wire integration test against actual Postgres — separate WIRE bead.
- Continuous sync between JSONL and Postgres — not in scope; this is one-shot migration.
- AxonStore itself — implemented in AX (`ddx-9c5bca8f`).

# Acceptance criteria

1. New file `cli/internal/bead/internal/storage/import_postgres.go` (or equivalent) implements the JSONL→Postgres importer. Uses `axonStore.Create` + `axonStore.Apply` for inserts + event appends.
2. Existing `Migrator.MigrateToAxon` method returns the real importer's result (not `ErrDeprecated`).
3. CLI flags wired: `--to-axon --dry-run`, `--to-axon --apply`, `--to-axon --verify`. Test: `TestImporter_DryRun_CountsOnly`, `TestImporter_Apply_WritesToPostgres`, `TestImporter_Verify_DetectsDrift`.
4. Idempotency: re-running `--apply` on an already-imported corpus is a no-op (skips conflicts). Test: `TestImporter_Apply_Idempotent_OnReRun`.
5. Field-fidelity: every JSONL bead field is preserved in Postgres, including `extra` preserved-keys. Test: `TestImporter_PreservesExtras`.
6. Event ordering: events imported preserve monotonic `created_at` (TD-027 §11.2 invariant 8). Test: `TestImporter_PreservesEventOrdering`.
7. Attachment migration: sidecar files under `.ddx/attachments/<bead>/` are uploaded to Unity Catalog Volumes (or local-equivalent for testing). Test: `TestImporter_MigratesAttachments`.
8. Verification mode: post-import, sample N beads, read back from AxonStore, assert equality with source. Test: `TestImporter_Verify_RoundTripPassesOnCleanImport`.
9. `cd cli && go test ./...` is green (with httptest-served Axon-shaped GraphQL endpoint or in-memory backend).
10. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
