description:
PROBLEM
TD-027 §21 requires physical impossibility of storage bypass, but the concrete storage implementations are still publicly importable from github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/ddx/internal/bead. Any package under cli/internal can name bead.Store, bead.JSONLBackend, bead.ExternalBackend, and AxonBackend directly, so the boundary is still convention-based.

ROOT CAUSE with file:line
- cli/internal/bead/store.go:40 declares public type Store in package bead.
- cli/internal/bead/backend_jsonl.go:18 declares public type JSONLBackend in package bead.
- cli/internal/bead/backend_external.go:21 declares public type ExternalBackend in package bead.
- cli/internal/bead/axon_backend.go:63 declares public type AxonBackend in package bead.
- cli/internal/bead/internal/storage/store.go:5 currently aliases bead.Store instead of owning the concrete implementation, so Go internal rules do not protect the concrete.
- cli/internal/bead/internal/storage/backend_jsonl.go:5 and backend_external.go:5 alias public concrete backend types instead of hiding them.

PROPOSED FIX
Move concrete storage implementation files from cli/internal/bead/ into cli/internal/bead/internal/storage/ so Store, JSONLBackend, ExternalBackend, and AxonBackend are defined only in the internal storage package. Leave package bead as the public interface/factory surface: Backend, ReadOnlyBackend, sub-interfaces, NewStore/NewStoreWithCollection, StoreFactory, and any required opaque constructor functions. Update imports inside cli/internal/bead/ to use internal/storage only from the bead package, preserving public behavior while making direct external imports fail under Go internal rules.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not narrow command, metrics, agent, or server callers except for compile breaks caused by this relocation; those caller sweeps are assigned to sibling children.
- Do not relocate lifecycle WatcherHub; that is assigned to a sibling child.
- Do not remove transitional lint analyzers or update TD-027 lint prose; that is assigned to the boundary-test/docs child.
- Do not change JSONL wire format, bd/br interchange behavior, archive policy, claim semantics, queue semantics, or migration semantics.
- Do not implement AxonStore/AxonBackend feature work beyond moving the existing concrete behind the boundary.
- Do not manually edit .ddx/beads.jsonl.
- Do not fix unrelated provider-launch/orphan integration flakes; if cd cli && go test ./... is blocked by pre-existing failures, report exact failing Test* names and leave this child’s changes otherwise verified.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
- TD-027 §21 Module Boundary / Boundary Lockdown.

PARENT/DEPS
- Parent: ddx-74452926.
- Depends on completion of caller narrowing children and on foundation ddx-c6317784 plus parent dependency beads ddx-3af1c1a6, ddx-71d3a2de, ddx-0ab16765, and ddx-9c5bca8f where applicable.

description:
PROBLEM
Reusable attempt workspace telemetry can report hit and miss behavior without quantifying conservative time-saved or bytes-saved estimates, leaving operators unable to evaluate whether project-local sequential reuse reduced repeated cold lefthook and Rust build costs.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares and cleans up workspaces without emitting savings values.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` historically did not expose reusable slot outcome metadata that can carry savings estimate inputs.
- No savings counters exist in the attempt path, leaving no signal for cold starts, time saved, or bytes saved.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace hit and miss telemetry events", sibling child "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", sibling child "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", sibling child "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation", child "attempt-backend: calculate reusable workspace savings estimates from allocation outcomes", and child "attempt-backend: emit zero reusable workspace savings for cold-start attempts". Extend the existing execution event/observability path so reused workspace attempts emit conservative time-saved and bytes-saved values from reusable allocation outcome data. Ensure the combined telemetry event carries slot hit/miss counts plus savings estimates for both reused and cold-start attempts, with cold-start values remaining zero.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.
- Do not alter the estimate formula except as needed to consume the contract delivered by the savings-estimate child.

description:
PROBLEM
While the managed worker evaluated readiness for ddx-e6abf4a6 on 2026-07-13, Codex PID 1135650 ran for more than 48 seconds but ddx work status --json reported active_work.count=1, bead_ids=[], and no provider_children. Unlike preclaim decomposition, this readiness hook runs after the bead claim and is supposed to heartbeat the owned lease, yet operators still cannot associate its provider CPU or elapsed time with the bead. A cancelled intake can also leave provider descendants outside the later attempt cleanup boundary.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2857-2892 claims the bead, emits readiness progress, and wraps PreClaimIntakeHook in work.WithHeartbeat. However the sidecar attempt/candidate identity is not set until cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3482-3487, after intake completes. cli/internal/agent/work/heartbeat.go:26-47 only calls reporter.OnTick and cannot populate a bead ID, phase, or provider probe route into an empty reporter. runPreClaimIntakeHookWithTimeout bounds the hook, but this call site has no provider-process baseline or explicit descendant reaping before implementation-attempt cleanup becomes active.

PROPOSED FIX
- Before dispatching claimed pre-dispatch intake, publish transient liveness containing bead ID, phase=pre_claim_intake, empty implementation attempt ID, and provider-child observations.
- Preserve the existing configured preclaim timeout and strict/warn-only readiness policy. On timeout or cancellation, terminate and reap only provider descendants introduced after the intake baseline.
- Clear transient intake state on every return before either parking the bead or establishing implementation-attempt liveness.
- Preserve claim heartbeat semantics and event ordering; intake remains pre-attempt and must not create an implementation attempt or cost record.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change readiness classification, strict-intake policy, claim timing, provider routing, post-attempt triage owned by ddx-2d76a4bb, or preclaim decomposition owned by ddx-092f0d34. Do not terminate provider processes that predate intake or belong to another worker.

description:
PROBLEM
Every place in the codebase that writes to .ddx/<something> today hardcodes filepath.Join(projectRoot, ".ddx", ...). This makes it impossible to relocate the DDx state to an XDG location for convention-mode projects without auditing and rewriting every call site. A leaked path means the convention-mode invariant ("no files written to project tree without a .ddx/ folder") breaks the moment that code path runs.

The full enumeration of touched paths is at minimum:
- .ddx/config.yaml
- .ddx/beads.jsonl
- .ddx/beads-archive.jsonl
- .ddx/attachments/<id>/
- .ddx/executions/<run-id>/
- .ddx/run-state/<id>.json
- .ddx/metrics/attempts.jsonl
- .ddx/.git-tracker.lock
- .ddx/plugins/<name>/
- .ddx/workers/<id>/
- .ddx/agent-logs/
- .ddx/scratch/
- and likely 10+ more across cli/internal/server/, cli/cmd/, library/checks/, scripts/

ROOT CAUSE
There is no single accessor that returns "the DDx root for this project". cli/internal/config/ has GetMetaPrompt() and similar config getters, but no DDxRoot(ctx) function. Every path-writer reaches into the file system directly.

PROPOSED FIX
1. Add a new package cli/internal/ddxroot with a single public function: `Path(ctx context.Context, projectRoot string) string`. Today returns filepath.Join(projectRoot, ".ddx"); a follow-up bead (E2) extends it to fall back to XDG when projectRoot/.ddx does not exist.
2. Audit every Go file in cli/ that contains the literal ".ddx" as a path segment. Replace `filepath.Join(projectRoot, ".ddx", ...)` with `filepath.Join(ddxroot.Path(ctx, projectRoot), ...)`. The audit must cover cli/cmd/, cli/internal/, library/checks/ (where applicable to ddx-side paths).
3. Add a build-time linter check (or a pre-commit hook lint rule) that fails the build if a new `filepath.Join.*"\\.ddx"` literal appears outside cli/internal/ddxroot/. Use go vet via a custom analyzer OR a simple ripgrep-based pre-commit hook (lefthook).
4. The resolver MUST NOT change behaviour in this bead: for any projectRoot today, ddxroot.Path returns exactly filepath.Join(projectRoot, ".ddx"). This bead is a pure refactor — no functional change.
5. Existing tests must continue to pass without modification. If any test fails, it has hardcoded .ddx in a way that bypassed the resolver — fix that test.

NON-SCOPE
- XDG fallback path (E2 bead).
- Convention mode bootstrap (E2 bead).
- `ddx init --global` (E3 bead).
- Manifest overlay (E5 bead).
- Migration of existing data (none required; behaviour is identical).

DEPS
None. This is the foundational refactor that the rest of the epic builds on.

acceptance:
1. `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go` no longer defines `StoreFactory`, `WatcherHub`, `NewWatcherHub`, `projectWatcher`, or `genLifecycleEventID`.
2. The public `bead` package still defines `LifecycleEvent` and the `LifecycleSubscriber` interface remains available from `cli/internal/bead/backend.go:144-147`.
3. `rg "bead\.NewWatcherHub|bead\.WatcherHub|bead\.StoreFactory|NewWatcherHub" cli/internal` shows production callers use `internal/lifecycle.NewWatcherHub` and no public bead concrete hub constructor remains.
4. `TestWatcherHub_SubscribeLifecycle` and `TestWatcherHub_PropagatesFactoryErrors` pass from `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/...` after the public symbols are removed.
5. `cd cli && go test ./internal/bead/... ./internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/... ./internal/server/...` passes, or the attempt records the sandbox-only `httptest` listener denial for `./internal/server/...` with the exact failing test names and still passes `cd cli && go test ./internal/bead/... ./internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/...`.
6. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
description:
PROBLEM
After the concrete watcher hub exists in `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/`, `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:23-100` must stop exporting `StoreFactory`, `WatcherHub`, and `NewWatcherHub` from the public `bead` package. Leaving those symbols in place keeps the construction path TD-027 §21 is trying to close.

ROOT CAUSE
The public `bead` package currently mixes the stable lifecycle event boundary with concrete polling implementation details in `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:23-224`. The stable public surface should be limited to `LifecycleEvent` and `LifecycleSubscriber`, while the hub implementation should be imported from the internal lifecycle package by allowed internal callers.

PROPOSED FIX
Delete the public concrete watcher definitions from `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go`, leaving `LifecycleEvent` in the public `bead` package and preserving `LifecycleSubscriber` at `cli/internal/bead/backend.go:144-147`. Update all in-repository callers that currently use `bead.NewWatcherHub`, `bead.WatcherHub`, or `bead.StoreFactory` to import and use `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle` instead. Do not change event payload shape or subscriber semantics.

Parent: ddx-74452926. Original parent dependency ID: ddx-27769c99. Governing artifact: TD-027 §21. No additional parent dependency IDs were supplied.

NON-SCOPE
- Storage backend relocation.
- Caller-field narrowing.
- Boundary import test.
- Lint analyzer cleanup.
- Rewriting watcher polling behavior beyond package relocation.

description:
PROBLEM
Fifteen DDx beads remained status=blocked after a transient host /tmp ENOSPC condition cleared. The queue stayed at zero ready until an operator manually reopened every bead, even though the existing execution resource preflight could prove the host was healthy.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:6605-6626 persists status: blocked output as only a free-text ExternalBlockerReason. cli/internal/bead/recheck.go:35-41 and 88-97 recheck only structured cross-repo refs and classify every other blocker as manual. The watch loop therefore has no safe, typed predicate for retrying local resource blockers.

PROPOSED FIX
- Persist a typed local resource-blocker marker when a blocked outcome is attributable to DDx resource preflight or an explicit machine-readable no_changes blocker kind.
- Re-run the same resource preflight on the idle path and reopen only matching typed blockers after it passes.
- Emit durable recheck evidence and preserve manual handling for all untyped blockers.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not parse arbitrary blocker prose for ENOSPC strings.
- Do not reopen cross-repo, provider, acceptance, test-suite, or operator-decision blockers.
- Do not change online/offline claim coordination owned by ddx-635ae251.

PARENT
Root reliability epic.

DEPS
No deps.
title: Epic: self-heal resolved local resource blockers

3. TestRunRecordSchemaRoundTrip covers version, run ID, bead ID, attempt ID, lifecycle phase, timestamps, and typed outcome fields without concrete harness-routing policy.

5. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/server/... passes.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.

cli/internal/server/state_runs.go:15-55 defines legacy run roots and lines 295-317 synthesize from sessions; no .ddx/runs/<id>/record.json writer exists. Phase 3 WB-2 specifies the missing substrate at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase3-server-rebuild-plan-2026-07-13.md:104-149.

Define the versioned DDx run-record schema and atomic writer. Create the record before Fizeau dispatch, then update the same record through attempt phases using write-fsync-rename discipline and stable DDx attempt identifiers.

Phase 1 typed Fizeau result contract and Phase 0 safe execution exit.

title: runs: publish one atomic record before Fizeau dispatch
work-last-detail: session closed before Stop hook

acceptance:
1. All 15 children closed.
2. ExecuteBeadWorker.Run replaced by work.Worker.Drain (~30 lines).
3. 18 store-error-as-loop-exit smells eliminated; transient store error during outcome-commit logs and continues.
4. attempted/hookFailed maps deleted; pick derives exclusion from drain.result.
5. Routing preflight runs once at Drain startup, never per iteration.
6. ddx work mode semantics preserved: default is drain-until-no-ready-work; --once runs one ready bead then exits; --watch stays alive and sleeps for the idle interval when no execution-ready beads exist; --idle-interval without --watch is a usage error; no public compatibility alias remains for the removed polling flag.
7. ddx try <bead-id> CLI command exists.
8. File/identifier rename per package split complete; ExecuteBead* shims deleted.
9. JSONL event shapes (bead.result, execute-bead, review, routing, triage-decision, loop-error) unchanged - verified by C0 fixture baseline.
10. Server worker integration (cli/internal/server/) compiles and behaves identically except for the explicit once/drain/watch mode contract; tests green at every phase.
11. ddx-c6e3db02, ddx-b24e9630, ddx-cfedee8e, ddx-a8718bec, ddx-dc157075, ddx-f9acb86d, ddx-7dcbd40b, ddx-8b7ed960, and ddx-dc300be9 behaviors preserved per C5/C9/C10 absorption ACs.
12. FEAT-006 + FEAT-010 cross-refs updated to reflect new package paths and the mode + idle_interval worker-loop vocabulary.
description:
ExecuteBeadWorker.Run() is a 700-line function with 24 returns: 4 legitimate terminal exits, 1 legacy idle-loop exit, 1 routing-preflight-kills-worker exit, and 18 store-error escalations from the same handleOutcomeStoreError pattern repeated across outcome paths. The implicit state machine in the loop is real and coherent (Pick -> Gate -> Claim -> Execute -> Classify -> Reviewing -> Terminal) but written as conditional soup instead of explicit state.

## Three-package split aligned to FEAT-010

  cli/internal/agent/run/   - Layer 1: invocation atom (existing dispatch + runner)
  cli/internal/agent/try/   - Layer 2: bead attempt (worktree, prompt, single Execute, Land, conflict-recovery, post-merge review, triage)
  cli/internal/agent/work/  - Layer 3: queue drain (pick, claim, heartbeat, drain-loop control, stop conditions)

try.Attempt(beadID) returns sealed Outcome { Disposition (enum), Cooldown, ParkReason, RecordEvents }. Loop becomes approximately 30 lines: pick -> guard -> claim -> attemptWithHeartbeat -> applyOutcome. Single commitOutcome helper deletes the 18 store-error returns.

## Ordering: refactor-LAST per user decision

In-flight Group A beads (c6e3db02 rate-limit, b24e9630 no_changes, cfedee8e ladder wire, a8718bec cost-cap reviewer) land first against current code. dc157075 tactical worker-stay-alive lands first as operational bridge. The stdout/watch-mode beads (ddx-7d9e1e82, ddx-f9acb86d, ddx-7dcbd40b, ddx-8b7ed960, ddx-dc300be9) define the public work-loop contract this refactor must preserve. description:
EPIC

Eliminate the .ddx/ footprint from arbitrary git repos using DDx, while keeping today's in-tree behavior available for projects that want it (DDx itself, HELIX, etc.). Make init effectively touchless: zero ceremony for the common case.

DESIGN PRINCIPLE

Single rule: presence of <project>/.ddx/ determines the DDx root.
- If <project>/.ddx/ exists → in-tree mode. Root = <project>/.ddx/. Operator commits or gitignores per their own .gitignore. DDx never manipulates .gitignore.
- If <project>/.ddx/ does NOT exist → convention mode. Root = ${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/ (defaults to ~/.local/share/ddx/projects/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/). The XDG directory is itself a git repo containing all DDx state for that project; the project's own git repo stays pristine.

PROJECT ID is the human-readable remote URL host/owner/repo triple, parsed from `git remote get-url origin`. SSH URLs (`git@github.com:easel/ddx.git`) and HTTPS URLs both resolve to the same path. Projects without a remote fall back to `local/<basename>-<abs-path-short-hash>/`. The slashes are filesystem-real, so the XDG path is browsable: `~/.local/share/ddx/projects/github.com/easel/ddx/`.

OVERRIDE PRECEDENCE at command time:
1. In-tree (<project>/.ddx/config.yaml) — top priority
2. Global (${XDG_DATA_HOME}/ddx/global/config.yaml) — installed by `ddx init --global`
3. Convention defaults — baked into the binary

Each layer is a delta on the one below. A project with no overrides commits zero new files and writes zero files into its worktree.

ENGINEERING IMPERATIVE

EVERY path in the codebase that today reads or writes under .ddx/ must route through a single DDxRoot(ctx) resolver. No filepath.Join(projectRoot, ".ddx", ...) calls outside that resolver. A regression linter asserts this invariant. The audit is the hard part of this epic.

KNOWN-HARD QUESTION (worth solving but not blocking):

When multiple worktrees of the same project (same remote URL) exist on one machine — e.g. `~/Projects/ddx` and `~/work/ddx-experiment` — they share the same XDG state. SHAs in events are unambiguous, but operator UX for "where do I cd to inspect this" is. Solution direction: each XDG project keeps a worktrees.json registry. One entry is marked master (operator pin or first-seen). Cross-references in audit logs and bead show output cite the master path.

CHILD BEADS

- E1: config: DDxRoot resolver + audit every .ddx/ path writer
- E2: config: convention mode bootstrap (XDG git repo + worktree registry)
- E3: config: ddx init --global installs user-tier skills/personas
- E4: config: ddx init creates .ddx/ in project, switches to in-tree mode
- E5: config: optional .ddx/config.yaml overlay for per-project overrides

NON-SCOPE
- Migration of existing in-tree repos (today's DDx repo, HELIX) is a separate concern. They stay in-tree mode by virtue of having .ddx/ already.
- Server-backed state (federation) is orthogonal. XDG state can be a git repo with a remote; pushing that remote IS the team-share mechanism.
- Manifest-only mode is rejected — the convention/in-tree split makes a separate manifest file unnecessary.

description:
PROBLEM
The candidate-cycle abstraction has deterministic Checks and Repair seams, but production wires only Reviewer. The real repository gate runs after LLM review and a failure immediately preserves the candidate; the existing RepairContext is ignored. DDx therefore neither checks before review nor asks Fizeau to repair a fixable gate failure in the same attempt workspace.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:376-389 constructs applyWorkerCandidateCycle with Reviewer and NoReview while Checks and Repair are nil.
- cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:475-491 and cli/cmd/try.go:452-467 run checks after candidate review.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:390-467 preserves a failed repository gate without a repair operation.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_post_review.go:398-417 creates RepairContext, but execute_bead_loop.go:4207-4236 does not execute it.
- cli/internal/agent/repair_prompt.go:8-70 lacks the full original task, current diff, and deterministic failure output required for an executable repair request.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the production candidate cycle so deterministic repository checks run before review. On a fixable check or review failure, submit a fresh public Fizeau Execute operation in the same DDx attempt worktree using the original task, current diff, and failure evidence. Preserve the primary operation MinPower and immutable operator passthrough exactly; do not set a concrete route. Append the repair commit, rerun checks, then review. Keep the repair budget bounded and durable in attempt evidence.

NON-SCOPE
Do not invent or call a Continue or resume API, invoke a provider CLI, raise power inside the current attempt, change Fizeau internals, or implement new-attempt escalation policy.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-b8cacbeb. Depends on ddx-8bcf71e0 so repair inherits the route-neutral reviewer and immutable passthrough contract.

1. `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/watcher_hub.go` exists, declares package `lifecycle`, and contains the concrete hub plus per-project watcher internals formerly in `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:23-224`.
2. `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go` no longer defines `StoreFactory`, `WatcherHub`, `NewWatcherHub`, `projectWatcher`, or `genLifecycleEventID`; the public `bead` package still defines `LifecycleEvent` and the `LifecycleSubscriber` interface.

description:
PROBLEM
`cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:23-100` defines and exports `StoreFactory`, `WatcherHub`, and `NewWatcherHub` from the public `bead` package, while `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:109-224` keeps the polling `projectWatcher` internals in the same public package. TD-027 §21 requires the concrete lifecycle polling hub to sit behind an internal boundary, but callers can still import the public bead package and construct the hub directly.

ROOT CAUSE
The concrete watcher implementation lives in `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go:23-224` instead of `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/`, so the concrete type and constructor are part of the public `bead` package API. The public interface boundary already exists at `cli/internal/bead/backend.go:144-147`, but the implementation is not separated from it.

PROPOSED FIX
Move the concrete watcher implementation from `cli/internal/bead/watcher.go` to `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/watcher_hub.go` with package name `lifecycle`. Keep `LifecycleEvent` in the public `bead` package, update the internal lifecycle implementation to reference `bead.LifecycleEvent`, and keep `LifecycleSubscriber` as the public interface. Move or rewrite watcher tests under `cli/internal/bead/internal/lifecycle/` so behavior is proven against the relocated implementation.

Parent: ddx-74452926. Governing artifact: TD-027 §21. No additional parent dependency IDs were supplied.

NON-SCOPE
- Storage backend relocation.
- Caller-field narrowing.
- Boundary import test.
- Lint analyzer cleanup.

1. TestDDXScratchTempDirUsesConfiguredExecutionRoot proves a DDx scratch temp helper creates ddx-home/provider-shim style directories under the configured execution/runtime root when configured.
2. TestDDXScratchTempDirFallsBackToOSTempDirWithoutConfiguredRoot proves fallback behavior remains when no project/config root is available.
3. TestProviderShimUsesDDXScratchRoot proves EnsureProviderShimOnPATH can create ddx-provider-shim-* under the configured scratch root rather than raw /tmp.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/config/... ./internal/agent/... -run "TestDDXScratchTempDirUsesConfiguredExecutionRoot|TestDDXScratchTempDirFallsBackToOSTempDirWithoutConfiguredRoot|TestProviderShimUsesDDXScratchRoot" passes.
5. cd cli && go test ./internal/config/... ./internal/agent/... ./cmd/... passes.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
DDx-owned temporary homes, provider shims, and helper scratch are created directly under raw os.TempDir(), so /tmp remains the choke point even when DDx has a configured execution/runtime temp root with available space. The 2026-07-08 incident had /tmp at 100% inode use while the configured execution worktree root under /Users/erik/Projects/.ddx-exec-wt still had capacity.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:91 creates provider shims with os.MkdirTemp("", "ddx-provider-shim-").
cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:29 and runner_test.go:56 create ddx-home-* with os.MkdirTemp("", "ddx-home-"); equivalent command tests create the same prefix in cli/cmd/work_resource_exhausted_test.go:80, cli/cmd/try_test.go:823, and cli/cmd/doctor_test.go:85.
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:116 creates ddx-fixture-bin-* with os.MkdirTemp("", ...).
These producers bypass config.ExecutionScratchRoot / config.ExecutionWorktreeRoot and strand inode-heavy scratch under /tmp.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a shared helper for DDx-owned scratch temp dirs that prefers config.ExecutionScratchRoot(projectRoot) or the configured execution/runtime root when a project root is available, and falls back to os.TempDir() only when no configured root exists. Migrate provider shims and DDx-owned temp homes/fixture bins to the helper where production/runtime context is available. Keep tests hermetic by setting the helper root explicitly in tests.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go
- cli/internal/config/execution_worktree_root.go or a new scratch-temp helper package
- relevant tests in cli/internal/agent and cli/cmd

NON-SCOPE
Do not move claim-liveness in this bead; ddx-3986b89a covers claim heartbeat root selection. Do not change git worktree placement. Do not store long-lived user config in execution scratch. Do not require a project root for all tests; fallback behavior must remain.

description:
PROBLEM
Slot-backed preparation can create reusable workspaces, but execute-bead cleanup still follows the disposable-workspace success path. A successful attempt can destructively delete a healthy reusable slot instead of returning it to the pool.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` installs a cleanup defer that ends in `_ = attemptBackend.Cleanup(ctx, workspace)`, so healthy reusable workspaces are deleted after successful attempts rather than released for reuse.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1019-1031` writes per-attempt cleanup metadata into the workspace before cleanup, so release must happen only after the sibling scrub/quarantine path has removed per-attempt state and classified the slot as healthy.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, governing parent `ddx-28e969b1`, and sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". In `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go`, replace the successful-attempt destructive cleanup branch for reusable slot-backed workspaces with the sibling backend release contract: after per-attempt metadata is written and scrub/quarantine classifies the workspace as healthy, return the reusable slot to the pool instead of deleting it. Preserve the existing destructive cleanup path for non-reusable or non-slot-backed workspaces.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-8a78ee90 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Execute-bead agents are instructed to run `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then run `git commit`. The repository-installed Git pre-commit hook invokes Lefthook again on the same staged tree. During attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4`, a small containment patch ran the full staged `./cmd` plus `./internal/agent` race gate twice explicitly after one test correction, then `git commit` launched a third full pass on the identical final staged tree. The second explicit pass alone spent more than 18 minutes in `go test` output processing. This duplicate gate contract serializes the queue without adding evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2104-2113` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2137-2148` require rich and embedded agents to rerun `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then commit exactly once, without recognizing that the implementation commit invokes the installed hook.
- `lefthook.yml:205-216` maps staged Go files to package-wide race tests, so each duplicate invocation can repeat multi-minute `./cmd` and `./internal/agent` gates.
- `.git/hooks/pre-commit:11-18` invokes Lefthook for ordinary `git commit`, making a separately requested manual invocation redundant when the staged tree is unchanged.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the ordinary implementation commit hook the single authoritative staged pre-commit gate. Update both execute-bead prompt variants and integrity evidence so agents stage the exact commit set, run `git commit` normally, and treat the hook output/exit status from that commit as satisfying the bead’s `lefthook run pre-commit` acceptance criterion. If a workflow explicitly runs the hook before commit, reuse that success only when a content/config fingerprint proves the staged tree and hook inputs are identical; otherwise rerun. A failed hook must abort the commit and remain a failed gate.

NON-SCOPE
Using `--no-verify`, setting `LEFTHOOK=0`, weakening or removing repository hooks, reusing evidence after any staged-tree or hook-config change, caching across attempts, bypassing human commits, or changing which tests the hook selects.

PARENT
None; root worker-throughput regression observed while draining the Niflheim queue.

DEPS
Related to `ddx-2afca9c9` (test-output/runtime headroom) and `ddx-03568f89` (gate evidence); no implementation dependency.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `TestExecuteBeadImplementationCommit_HookFailureAbortsCommit` proves a nonzero hook blocks the commit, records failed gate evidence, and never retries with `--no-verify` or `LEFTHOOK=0`.
- `TestExecuteBeadPreCommitEvidence_InvalidatedByStagedMutation` proves any staged content or relevant hook-config change invalidates prior green evidence and requires a new hook run.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
Operators need conservative time-saved and bytes-saved estimates to appear in the execution observability stream for reuse-hit attempts, but reused workspace attempts currently only expose whether allocation hit or missed.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares reusable workspaces and runs cleanup without emitting savings values for reused attempts through the operator-visible execution observability path.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` historically did not provide allocation outcome metadata that could drive savings-bearing reuse telemetry.
- The attempt path lacks counters or event fields that turn carried savings values into operator-visible telemetry.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, parent `ddx-1436e204`, parent `ddx-5dda007b`, child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace hit and miss telemetry events", sibling child "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", sibling child "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", sibling child "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation", child "attempt-backend: calculate reusable workspace savings estimates from allocation outcomes", child "attempt-backend: emit zero reusable workspace savings for cold-start attempts", and child "attempt-backend: carry reusable workspace savings through execution telemetry". Publish the carried reusable workspace savings values through the execution observability path for reuse-hit attempts so operator-facing attempt events include nonzero conservative time-saved and bytes-saved estimates when the allocation outcome supplies them.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.
- Do not alter the estimate formula except as needed to consume the contract delivered by the savings-estimate child.
- Do not define cold-start zero behavior or reuse-win aggregation; those belong to separate child beads.

description:
PROBLEM
A single DDx attempt can monopolize the entire server-owned CPU allowance. On 2026-07-13, TestExecuteBead_ConcurrentWorkers_NoHEADRefRace launched five Codex providers whose aggregate use reached about 350 percent CPU, nearly saturating the installed server CPUQuota=400 percent. The aggregate service cap protected the host but provided no fairness between attempts, and a manual/offline worker outside ddx-server.service has no equivalent cap at all.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/cmd/server_service.go:98-102 exposes only an aggregate CPU quota and weight for the complete server-owned worker/provider/build tree. cli/internal/service/service.go:15-22 defines that policy explicitly as aggregate. cli/internal/agent/executor.go:177-188 starts each provider directly, while cli/internal/agent/executor_unix.go:10-29 configures only a process group and parent-death signal; no attempt-scoped CPU controller contains the provider and all descendants. Consequently one nested test/provider fanout can consume the whole managed-service budget, while the same manual worker path is unbounded.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add one attempt-scoped CPU-envelope abstraction at the provider execution boundary so the harness root and every descendant share a bounded controller. Membership must survive process-group/session changes, double-forking, and reparenting; cleanup and cancellation must act on controller membership rather than ancestry alone.
- Apply the same default and configuration to server-managed and manual/offline workers without requiring a live DDx server. Preserve the existing parent-death behavior so managed provider trees still die when their worker/server dies.
- Use a conservative default of 200 percent of one core per active attempt, allow an explicit 0 value to disable the per-attempt cap, and keep the existing aggregate server service cap as the outer ceiling.

When the platform cannot enforce a hard quota, continue with lowered scheduling priority and an operator-visible degraded-control event rather than silently claiming enforcement.

description:
PROBLEM
The normal internal/agent gate timed out after 10 minutes while TestLifecycleDispatchRejectsProjectRootMutation waited for captureLifecycleProjectStatus. One unbounded project-status subprocess can consume the complete package budget, fail unrelated beads, and force the queue to retry work whose focused acceptance tests are already green.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/lifecycle_dispatch.go:95-117 accepts no context. At line 105 it calls RepairKnownConfigCorruption with context.Background, and at line 110 it runs git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all with context.Background. The before, after, and restored snapshots at cli/internal/agent/lifecycle_dispatch.go:47, 144, and 157 therefore outlive caller cancellation and have no per-operation deadline. description:
PROBLEM
DDx can persist only a free-text external blocker reason or a structured cross-repo bead reference. Local resource failures therefore cannot be distinguished safely from manual blockers after the host recovers.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/bead/store.go:761-825 defines ExtraLifecycleExternalBlockerReason and ExtraLifecycleCrossRepoBlockerRef, but no typed local blocker representation. cli/internal/bead/store.go:852-870 clears cross-repo metadata on transition out of blocked but has no equivalent local-resource marker to validate or clear.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add a typed local blocker marker in cli/internal/bead/local_blocker.go with a closed enum containing local_resource_exhaustion, plus optional resource roots/fingerprint needed for recheck evidence.
- Add parse/validation helpers matching the CrossRepoBlockerRef pattern.
- Store the marker under a named Extra key and clear it on every transition out of blocked.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/bead/local_blocker.go
- cli/internal/bead/store.go

description:
PROBLEM
Cold-start and reusable-workspace miss attempts have no explicit zero-savings observability signal, so operators can mistake absent savings fields for missing telemetry instead of a deliberate non-reuse outcome.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares and cleans up workspaces without emitting savings values for either reused or cold-start workspaces.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` historically did not expose reusable slot outcome metadata that can carry savings estimate inputs.
- No savings counters exist in the attempt path, leaving no signal for cold starts, time saved, or bytes saved.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace hit and miss telemetry events", sibling child "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", sibling child "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", sibling child "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation", and child "attempt-backend: calculate reusable workspace savings estimates from allocation outcomes". Wire the zero-savings case into execute-bead orchestration so cold starts and reusable-workspace misses emit zero time-saved and zero bytes-saved through the existing execution event/observability path. Ensure these attempts are not counted as reuse wins and preserve the final telemetry contract chosen by the reusable workspace hit/miss telemetry child.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.
- Do not add non-zero savings emission for reused attempts in this child.

acceptance:
1. `TestExecuteBeadPrompt_UsesImplementationCommitAsSinglePreCommitGate` proves both rich and embedded prompts tell the agent to stage exact paths and rely on the normal commit hook once, without requesting a separate identical staged `lefthook` run.
2. `TestExecuteBeadImplementationCommit_RunsPreCommitOnceForUnchangedIndex` uses an instrumented hook and proves one unchanged final staged tree produces exactly one hook invocation and one implementation commit.
3. `TestExecuteBeadImplementationCommit_HookFailureAbortsCommit` proves a nonzero hook blocks the commit, records failed gate evidence, and never retries with `--no-verify` or `LEFTHOOK=0`.
4. `TestExecuteBeadPreCommitEvidence_InvalidatedByStagedMutation` proves any staged content or relevant hook-config change invalidates prior green evidence and requires a new hook run.
5. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run "^(TestExecuteBeadPrompt_UsesImplementationCommitAsSinglePreCommitGate|TestExecuteBeadImplementationCommit_RunsPreCommitOnceForUnchangedIndex|TestExecuteBeadImplementationCommit_HookFailureAbortsCommit|TestExecuteBeadPreCommitEvidence_InvalidatedByStagedMutation)$" -count=1 -timeout 120s` passes.
6. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s` passes.
7. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Execute-bead agents are instructed to run `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then run `git commit`. The repository-installed Git pre-commit hook invokes Lefthook again on the same staged tree. During attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4`, a small containment patch ran the full staged `./cmd` plus `./internal/agent` race gate twice explicitly after one test correction, then `git commit` launched a third full pass on the identical final staged tree. The second explicit pass alone spent more than 18 minutes in `go test` output processing. This duplicate gate contract serializes the queue without adding evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2104-2113` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2137-2148` require rich and embedded agents to rerun `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then commit exactly once, without recognizing that the implementation commit invokes the installed hook.
- `lefthook.yml:205-216` maps staged Go files to package-wide race tests, so each duplicate invocation can repeat multi-minute `./cmd` and `./internal/agent` gates.
- `.git/hooks/pre-commit:11-18` invokes Lefthook for ordinary `git commit`, making a separately requested manual invocation redundant when the staged tree is unchanged.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the ordinary implementation commit hook the single authoritative staged pre-commit gate. Update both execute-bead prompt variants and integrity evidence so agents stage the exact commit set, run `git commit` normally, and treat the hook output/exit status from that commit as satisfying the bead’s `lefthook run pre-commit` acceptance criterion. If a workflow explicitly runs the hook before commit, reuse that success only when a content/config fingerprint proves the staged tree and hook inputs are identical; otherwise rerun. A failed hook must abort the commit and remain a failed gate.

NON-SCOPE
Using `--no-verify`, setting `LEFTHOOK=0`, weakening or removing repository hooks, reusing evidence after any staged-tree or hook-config change, caching across attempts, bypassing human commits, or changing which tests the hook selects.

PARENT
None; root worker-throughput regression observed while draining the Niflheim queue.

DEPS
Related to `ddx-2afca9c9` (test-output/runtime headroom) and `ddx-03568f89` (gate evidence); no implementation dependency.

description:
PROBLEM
Reused attempts must emit the same combined reusable workspace telemetry event as cold-start attempts. Operators currently have to correlate separate hit/miss and savings signals to compare reused outcomes against cold starts.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares reusable workspaces and performs cleanup but does not emit one combined telemetry record that includes both reuse hit counts and savings values for reused attempts.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` exposes outcome metadata that can identify reusable workspace allocation results, but reused-attempt savings are not carried into the same emitted event as slot allocation counts.
- Attempt-path savings counters are not summarized with hit/miss counters, so reuse wins cannot be observed from one event.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, parent `ddx-1436e204`, parent `ddx-5dda007b`, child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace hit and miss telemetry events", sibling child "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", sibling child "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", sibling child "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation", child "attempt-backend: calculate reusable workspace savings estimates from allocation outcomes", child "attempt-backend: emit zero reusable workspace savings for cold-start attempts", child "attempt-backend: carry reusable workspace savings through execution telemetry", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace savings for reused attempts", child "attempt-backend: define combined reusable workspace telemetry payload", child "attempt-backend: emit combined reusable workspace telemetry for cold starts", and child "attempt-backend: carry reused workspace savings into combined telemetry inputs". Wire the reused-attempt telemetry input into the existing combined reusable workspace telemetry emission path so a reused attempt emits one event containing slot hit count, slot miss count, time-saved, and bytes-saved. Ensure the final event stream uses one shape for reuse and cold-start attempts.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Parent bead `ddx-54ff73df`: attempt-backend combined workspace hit, miss, and savings telemetry.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.
- Do not alter the estimate formula except as needed to consume the contract delivered by the savings-estimate child.
- Do not change the existing Docker attempt backend shared-cache behaviour while adding this event.

description:
PROBLEM
There is no lower-level contract that a producer of process-lifetime scratch directories can use to record durable ownership evidence, and that execution cleanup can read, without creating an import cycle between internal/testutils and internal/agent. Without this marker, a directory's name prefix plus age becomes the only signal available to cleanup, which cannot distinguish an abandoned directory from one still owned by a live long-running test process.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/testutils/fixture_repo.go:119-167 creates and publishes binary directories with no durable owner marker, so there is nothing for cleanup to key ownership on.
cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:667-681 synthesizes ownership only when cleanup.json is absent, and cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:189-221 preserves a directory with live PID or lease evidence only when compatible metadata already exists — no shared marker type exists that both a testutils producer and the agent cleaner can construct and validate.
ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93 establish host-global trust and metadata-marked reclamation rules but define no producer-writable process-lifetime ownership marker.

PROPOSED FIX
Add a small internal/scratchowner package that defines an owner-marker contract importable by both internal/testutils and internal/agent with no import cycle. The marker records: resource kind, owner PID, creation time, and a process-start identity when the platform exposes one. Provide atomic write (temp file + rename within the target directory) and a read/validate path that reports live, dead, or uncertain owner status consistent with the ownership rules in ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93. A prefix or name match is never treated as ownership proof.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- a new cli/internal/scratchowner package and its tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not modify fixture_repo.go producers or execution_cleanup.go in this bead; child beads ddx (fixture producers) and ddx (cleanup wiring) consume this contract.
Do not change Fizeau routing, test-seam behavior, harness selection, model selection, or provider policy.
Do not redesign general host-global scratch trust; ddx-05e3d16b and ddx-1eb1ba93 own that policy.
Do not change execution scratch placement; ddx-b2702b9f owns that migration.

PARENT
ddx-f914dddd

DEPS
ddx-1eb1ba93 must land first so metadata-marked reclamation and host-global ownership rules are established; it already depends on ddx-05e3d16b.

description:
PROBLEM
Execute-bead orchestration cannot emit reliable reusable-workspace hit/miss telemetry because the attempt backend resolution path does not return structured metadata describing whether a reusable workspace slot was hit, missed, cold-started, or how much prior state was reused.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` (`ResolveAttemptBackend`) exposes no reusable slot outcome metadata to the execution path.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares and cleans up workspaces but has no typed allocation outcome to associate with the resolved backend policy or worker-slot identity.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, and the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". Add a small typed reusable-workspace outcome surface to the attempt backend path that records the resolved reusable-workspace policy, project identity, worker-slot identity, hit/miss/cold-start classification, and estimated reusable state inputs needed by telemetry. Wire worktree and local-clone preparation through that surface without changing backend selection semantics.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.

description:
PROBLEM
A watch worker can prove its temp/evidence roots are healthy on every dispatch, yet beads previously blocked by local resource exhaustion remain outside candidate selection forever. This required manually reopening fifteen beads after the July 11 ENOSPC incident.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2352-2363 performs an idle-path auto-reopen only for retryable provider-connectivity proposals before nextCandidate. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:2492-2576 reports and sleeps on no ready work without rechecking blocked local resources. cli/internal/agent/execution_resources.go:208-300 already supplies the authoritative root health probe, but the idle lifecycle path never applies it to typed blocked beads.

PROPOSED FIX
- Before candidate selection in watch mode, list blocked beads carrying the typed local_resource_exhaustion marker from ddx-c4cbf253.
- Run the configured ExecutionResourceChecker once per idle pass. Reopen all matching beads through LifecycleTransitionOptions{ManualReopen:true} only when the probe is healthy.
- Append durable local_resource_blocker_recheck evidence containing before/after root checks and emit a loop event.
- Leave typed blockers blocked when the probe is unhealthy and leave every untyped/manual blocker untouched.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_resource_exhausted_test.go or one focused companion test

NON-SCOPE
- Do not parse free-text blocker reasons.
- Do not reopen cross-repo, provider, test-suite, or operator-decision blockers.
- Do not change resource thresholds or cleanup policy.

PARENT
- ddx-5958e8a4.

- ddx-c4cbf253 persists the typed marker.

description:
PROBLEM
With the slot pool, reuse/scrub path, and preserved build state implemented in the sibling children, the production execute-bead path still prepares a throwaway workspace per attempt and defers destructive cleanup, so no real bead benefits and operators have no visibility into whether reuse is happening or what it saves.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares a workspace with `attemptBackend.Prepare(...)` for every attempt and installs a `defer` that ends in `_ = attemptBackend.Cleanup(ctx, workspace)`, treating the workspace as disposable; the only preservation branch is `runtime.PreserveAttemptWorktree` for the worktree backend.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1019-1031` (`WriteExecutionCleanupMetadata`) writes per-attempt metadata into the workspace, which must be scrubbed on reuse rather than carried into the next bead.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` (`ResolveAttemptBackend`) constructs backends without any pool handle or worker-slot identity, so orchestration has nothing to thread through.
- No hit/miss or savings counters exist anywhere in the attempt path, so there is no signal that would have surfaced the Niflheim cold-build amplification (roughly 20-24 minutes per bead in cold lefthook/clippy runs).

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". Thread the resolved reusable-workspace policy and worker-slot identity from `ResolveAttemptBackend` into both the linked-worktree and local-clone backends so production preparation goes through the bounded slot allocator. Replace the unconditional destructive cleanup in the `execute_bead.go` defer with a release that returns a healthy slot to the pool and only deletes on quarantine, while preserving existing `PreserveAttemptWorktree`, `KeepOnError`, evidence-preservation, and the `resource_exhausted` classification of `Prepare` failures. Emit reuse telemetry — slot hit/miss counts plus time and bytes saved — through the existing execution event/observability path so operators can see reuse behaviour per project and worker.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.

description:
PROBLEM
Production execute-bead orchestration cannot route linked-worktree or local-clone attempts through the reusable slot pool because the selected attempt backend does not carry the resolved reusable-workspace policy or worker-slot identity.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` (`ResolveAttemptBackend`) constructs linked-worktree and local-clone attempt backends without threading a reusable-workspace policy, slot pool handle, or worker-slot identity into those implementations.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` therefore receives a backend whose `Prepare(...)` method has no production-visible way to choose bounded slot allocation for eligible attempt modes.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af` and the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". Update `ResolveAttemptBackend` and the linked-worktree/local-clone backend constructors or option structs so they accept the resolved reusable-workspace policy, slot allocator handle, and worker-slot identity. Keep Docker backend construction unchanged except for any no-op plumbing needed by shared interfaces. Add focused tests proving both eligible backend types receive the policy and slot identity used later by preparation.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx still chooses or biases concrete Fizeau routes in production even after removing the obvious run/try/work preflight. Local harness-name dispatch, lifecycle profile discovery, server defaults, project-model inheritance, and dead exported route-control APIs let DDx select harness/provider/model/profile policy it does not own. Removing preflight also left the advertised 60s route-resolution lease guard disconnected.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:90-135, cli/internal/agent/dispatch.go:36-67, and cli/internal/agent/runner.go:84-114 route virtual/script names into DDx-local runners instead of forwarding an operator harness constraint to Fizeau.
- cli/internal/agent/preclaim_intake_hook.go:477-494,559-579 and cli/internal/agent/recovery_decompose.go:237-247 call ListPolicies/ListModels and select concrete lifecycle profiles.
- cli/internal/server/graphql_adapters.go:73-100, workers_supervisor.go:23-106, graphql/resolver_feat008.go:89-120, and the workers frontend seed default/smart profiles; server workers.go:363-372 and agent/run_dispatch_spec.go:103-127 leave opaque passthrough false, so config/resolved.go:73-80 can inject project agent.model into an unpinned request.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:6935-7533, service_run.go:461-636, cli/cmd/agent_execute_loop_escalation.go:104-379, internal/agent/escalation/ladder.go, and model_discovery_containment.go retain exclusion, resolver, catalog-ladder, historical-route-seeding, and discovery-control capabilities.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:88-91,215-228 plus work/try/server flag plumbing retain route-resolution-timeout after deleting its resolver call, making the documented lease-release guard a no-op.

PROPOSED FIX
Route every production agent and lifecycle invocation through Fizeau. Preserve explicit operator Harness, Provider, Model, Policy/Profile, MaxPower, and other public passthrough byte-for-byte, but never synthesize concrete route fields. Express DDx-owned difficulty or escalation only through abstract MinPower. Remove local script/virtual name dispatch from production, lifecycle catalog/profile selection, default/smart profile injection, project-model inheritance for opaque execution entry points, route exclusion/catalog/seed machinery, and dead exported control APIs. Retain the 60s wedge guard by timing only Fizeau's opaque route stage from Execute dispatch until its first routing_decision event; on expiry cancel the operation, release the lease, and append operator_attention, and permanently disarm the timer once routing_decision arrives.

NON-SCOPE
Do not remove read-only provider/model inventory or UI display of Fizeau-returned route evidence, change Fizeau internals, reject explicit operator passthrough, implement typed-result policy that requires a newer Fizeau release, or implement reviewer cardinality/stronger-review policy owned by dependent beads.

ddx-b8cacbeb.

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can leave normative requirements unmapped or map the same requirement more than once and still pass lint. An unmapped requirement means a Complete stamp covers work with no stated proof; a duplicated mapping hides which row is the authoritative evidence and inflates apparent coverage.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer package does not exist in this checkout — the expected path cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1 is absent (cli/tools/lint/ currently contains only evidencelint, routinglint, runtimelint). No pass performs coverage-cardinality arithmetic between a document's requirement inventory and its Verification mapping rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67 (every Complete/Implemented requirement or stable anchor covered exactly once) and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68 (uncovered and duplicate mappings must fail).

PROPOSED FIX
Consuming the Complete/Implemented document set from the scaffold/status-parser child and the requirement inventory plus mapping-rows model from the Verification mapping-parser child, add the coverage-cardinality pass: for each Complete/Implemented document, join inventory requirements/anchors against mapping rows by requirement identifier, emit one diagnostic per requirement covered zero times naming that requirement, and emit one diagnostic per requirement covered more than once naming that requirement as a duplicate mapping. A requirement covered exactly once yields no diagnostic. Follow the package and test conventions in cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go and cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer_test.go, including golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis and analysistest-style fixtures where applicable. The analyzer is read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement the zero-evidence (empty row set) diagnostic — that is the sibling zero-evidence child. Do not implement the file-only-citation exclusion rule — that is the sibling citation-granularity child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child; consume its model. Do not implement status parsing — that is the scaffold child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not resolve whether named Test* symbols, static checks, or artifacts exist — evidence-target resolution is a sibling child. Do not enforce the executable verification command allowlist — command allowlist enforcement is a sibling child.

DEPS: parent ddx-29449fa5 (and its parent ddx-471d66b6); the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

PROBLEM
The store/config helpers behind `execute_bead_loop_test.go` and `execute_bead_loop_disruption_test.go` can still inherit process-global DDx/config roots, which is what blocked the full-package proof.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE

- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_disruption_test.go:250-279 exercises the interrupted work path under the same helper and was the path that surfaced the host-dependent snapshot.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the loop/store helpers allocate private fixture/config roots, add a regression around `newExecuteLoopTestStore` or `runInterruptedWorkAttempt` if needed, and keep the interrupt and resource-preflight tests hermetic.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change interruption semantics, claim handling, or cleanup production code. Do not treat a killed, backgrounded, or incomplete run as success.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-8a78ee90 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 1 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Execute-bead agents are instructed to run `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then run `git commit`. The repository-installed Git pre-commit hook invokes Lefthook again on the same staged tree. During attempt `20260713T121749-836fcbe4`, a small containment patch ran the full staged `./cmd` plus `./internal/agent` race gate twice explicitly after one test correction, then `git commit` launched a third full pass on the identical final staged tree. The second explicit pass alone spent more than 18 minutes in `go test` output processing. This duplicate gate contract serializes the queue without adding evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2104-2113` and `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2137-2148` require rich and embedded agents to rerun `lefthook run pre-commit` after staging and then commit exactly once, without recognizing that the implementation commit invokes the installed hook.

2. TestReviewTransportErrorDowngradesNotFails injects the typed cause twice and proves an operator-visible review-downgraded event plus deterministic-only close, without implementation failure or parking.
3. TestNonTransportReviewErrorDoesNotMasqueradeAsTransport proves semantic and DDx-stage failures do not take the transport retry/downgrade path.
4. TestReviewTransportPolicyDoesNotParseText supplies transport-looking provider text under a non-transport typed cause and proves the typed cause alone controls policy.
5. rg -n "ClassifyReviewError|reviewer.*SelectStrongestProfile|reviewer.*LoadProfileSnapshot" cli/internal/agent --glob "*.go" returns no production text/profile transport policy.
6. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/escalation/... ./cmd/... -run "Test(ReviewTransportRetryKeepsPowerAndPins|ReviewTransportErrorDowngradesNotFails|NonTransportReviewErrorDoesNotMasqueradeAsTransport|ReviewTransportPolicyDoesNotParseText)" -count=1 passes.
7. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/escalation/... ./cmd/... -count=1 -timeout 600s passes.
8. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
DDx currently guesses that reviewer errors are transport failures from error strings, raises reviewer power/profile on retry, and ultimately fails or parks otherwise valid implementation work. The design requires Fizeau to classify its own terminal transport outcome; DDx may retry one review operation at identical power and passthrough, then downgrade to deterministic-only close with operator-visible evidence.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:7949-7991 ClassifyReviewError uses text and defaults unknown errors to transport.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:869-931 increases MinPower and selects top profiles after prior errors.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_review.go:1251-1292 and execute_bead_review_group.go:153-175 return dispatch errors as review failures.
- cli/internal/agent/candidate_cycle.go:315-325 converts any reviewer error to review_malfunction and prevents landing.
- Current pinned Fizeau v0.14.50 in cli/go.mod exposes no typed Cause/Stage field, so this change must wait for ddx-66a8883f and its compatible upstream release/conformance proof.

PROPOSED FIX
Consume the single typed Fizeau terminal review-transport cause from the DDx attempt-policy adapter. Retry exactly once at identical MinPower and byte-identical operator passthrough. If the typed transport failure repeats, emit an operator-visible review-downgraded event and allow deterministic-checks-only close. Do not raise power, select a profile, or fail the implementation because review transport is unavailable. Non-transport review errors remain distinct and follow their typed policy.

NON-SCOPE
Do not classify provider text, implement Fizeau provider retry, add continuation, invoke provider CLIs, or weaken semantic BLOCK/REQUEST_CHANGES findings.

PARENT AND DEPS
Parent: ddx-b8cacbeb. Depends on ddx-642a9f26 plus ddx-66a8883f, the blocked typed Fizeau result consumer. It must not become execution-ready until the compatible upstream contract is pinned and conformance is green.
title: review: consume typed Fizeau transport outcomes for retry and downgrade

2. TestServerStoresUseBackendInterfaces passes and verifies server/GraphQL resolver seams expose bead.Backend, bead.ReadOnlyBackend, or narrower interfaces rather than *bead.Store.
3. TestExecuteBeadLoopStoreDoesNotExposeConcreteStore passes and proves execute-loop dependencies can be satisfied without naming *bead.Store outside test construction helpers.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/server/... ./internal/escalation/... passes.
5. cd cli && go test ./... passes, or the attempt records exact pre-existing unrelated failing Test* symbols.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
TD-027 §21 requires the agent and server layers to compile against bead interface contracts before storage concretes are relocated. These packages still have many *bead.Store test fixtures, helper wrappers, and production escape hatches that make the later internal-package move too broad and fragile.

ROOT CAUSE with file:line
- cli/internal/server/workers.go:1580 accepts *bead.Store in staleDiskEntryCanReleaseClaim.
- cli/internal/server/graphql/ddxroot_paths.go:12 returns *bead.Store from projectBeadStore.
- cli/internal/server/graphql/resolver_mutation_beads.go:14 returns *bead.Store from mutationResolver.beadStore.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_integration_test.go:199 type-asserts a store back to *bead.Store.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:5896 documents deterministic ready-queue eligibility as bead.Store-specific instead of depending on an interface.
- Many agent/server test helpers still return *bead.Store, which prevents a package-level AST proof from staying small.

PROPOSED FIX
Update agent, agent/try, server, and server/graphql production code and test helpers to accept bead.Backend, bead.ReadOnlyBackend, or existing narrow sub-interfaces where the concrete is not required. Introduce local test-only fakes/adapters where a test currently embeds *bead.Store only to satisfy a small method set. Preserve concrete construction only at the package boundary where NewStore/NewStoreWithCollection is called.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not change command/metrics caller clusters assigned to the sibling caller-narrowing child.
- Do not move storage concrete definitions or aliases.
- Do not relocate lifecycle WatcherHub.
- Do not change queue semantics, claim semantics, retry policy, worker lifecycle policy, or GraphQL behavior except for type narrowing.
- Do not implement per-concern L/C/X/Q/D/A/MIG behavior or AxonStore/AxonBackend behavior.
- Do not manually edit .ddx/beads.jsonl.
- Do not fix unrelated provider-launch/orphan integration flakes; if cd cli && go test ./... is blocked by pre-existing failures, report exact failing Test* names and leave this child’s changes otherwise verified.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
- TD-027 §21 Module Boundary / Boundary Lockdown.

PARENT/DEPS
- Parent: ddx-74452926.
- Must be scheduled after foundation ddx-c6317784 and the per-concern dependency beads already referenced by the parent, including ddx-3af1c1a6, ddx-71d3a2de, ddx-0ab16765, and Axon follow-up ddx-9c5bca8f where applicable.

description: PROBLEM: on 2026-07-06..2026-07-19 two ddx drains of telepathdata/cayce silently forked the repo: one checkout had branch.master.merge=refs/heads/main while the repo default was refs/heads/master, so each worker fleet pushed commits AND the beads.jsonl tracker to a different remote branch for 13 days. Because the tracker lives in git, forking the branch forks the queue itself — both sides showed healthy progress, duplicated ~100 non-chore commits of work under different bead IDs, and nobody was alerted. Recovered manually on 2026-07-20 (archive branch + delete + port-audit bead cayce-30ea87db). ROOT CAUSE: ddx work/try honor whatever upstream the checkout is configured with and have no preflight check that the branch being drained is (or descends from) the remote's default branch (origin/HEAD). PROPOSED FIX: before claiming the first bead, ddx work (and ddx try) resolve origin/HEAD and compare with the current branch's upstream: hard-fail with a clear message when the upstream ref names a different branch than origin/HEAD (override flag, e.g. --allow-non-default-branch, for deliberate feature-branch drains); also warn when the local branch is behind its upstream at drain start. 2. TestLefthookGoTest_FromCliRootRemainsCompatible invokes the helper from cli/ with internal/agent/example.go and proves the same package command runs exactly once.
3. TestLefthookGoTest_UnmappedGoPathFailsClosed supplies an unmappable Go path and proves the helper exits nonzero with a diagnostic that names the rejected path.
4. TestLefthookGoTest_DeduplicatesPackageSelection supplies multiple Go files in one package and proves the package is tested once.
5. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run "^(TestLefthookGoTest_(FromRepoRootRunsInternalAgent|FromCliRootRemainsCompatible|UnmappedGoPathFailsClosed|DeduplicatesPackageSelection))$" -count=1 -timeout 60s passes.
6. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
The targeted Go pre-commit helper can report success without running any tests when it is invoked from the repository root with the same root-relative cli/... paths that Git and operator diagnostics naturally produce. During execute-bead attempt 20260713T171608-d879ec96, sh scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go returned 0 in 123ms and launched no go process, creating false validation evidence after the real package gate had timed out.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh:8-18 converts each input to a directory, strips a leading cli/, and silently continues when that derived directory does not exist relative to the current working directory. lefthook.yml:11-14 and lefthook.yml:205-216 normally run the helper with cli/ as the command root, but the helper neither establishes nor validates that working-directory contract. From the repository root, cli/internal/agent becomes internal/agent, the directory check fails, and the helper exits with its initial zero status.

PROPOSED FIX
Make the helper resolve the Go module root deterministically from its own repository location or explicitly normalize both repository-root cli/... paths and cli-root internal/... paths before selecting packages. Track every Go path supplied to the helper and fail nonzero with a diagnostic naming any path that cannot be mapped to an existing module package. Preserve targeted package selection, the race detector, the 30-minute per-package timeout, and compatibility with the normal Lefthook cli/ root.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- scripts/lefthook-go-test.sh
- lefthook.yml only if invocation wiring needs an explicit root argument
- a Go or shell-backed regression test under cli/internal/agent that runs the helper with a fake go executable and inspects its arguments

NON-SCOPE
Do not broaden the hook to the full repository, remove -race, raise or remove the timeout, silently ignore unmapped Go paths, or change which staged files Lefthook passes to the command.

PARENT
None; root hook-validation reliability defect discovered during the Niflheim queue drain.

DEPS
None. Related prior hook reliability work is ddx-42a86089; duplicate-hook work is ddx-8a78ee90.
