acceptance:
1. TestExecuteBead_ConcurrentWorkers_NoHEADRefRace continues to run five concurrent ExecuteBeadWithConfig calls against one real temporary Git repository and preserves the HEAD compare-and-swap and BaseRev assertions.
2. TestExecuteBead_ConcurrentWorkers_NoHEADRefRace_DoesNotSpawnProviders installs provider-spawn tripwires for codex, claude, gemini, and __provider-launch and proves none are invoked by the fixture.
3. The fixture uses a bounded hermetic AgentRunner implementation; it does not call NewRunner, production Fizeau discovery, network APIs, subscription caches, or real provider binaries.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent -run "^TestExecuteBead_ConcurrentWorkers_NoHEADRefRace(_DoesNotSpawnProviders)?$" -count=1 -timeout 30s passes.
5. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s passes and leaves no provider descendants whose command line references the test temp root.
6. A failure/timeout path test proves every fixture-owned subprocess is canceled and reaped before the test returns.
7. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Running the required cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... gate launches five real Codex provider processes from TestExecuteBead_ConcurrentWorkers_NoHEADRefRace. In the 2026-07-13 ddx-2502d3c6 attempt, the package test spawned PIDs 225004, 225054, 225173, 225576, and 226111 as __provider-launch ... codex exec; each ran for more than six minutes at about 10-12% CPU. The test package approached its 10-minute timeout, blocking the single queue worker and consuming server-cgroup CPU for a test whose stated concern is only parent-repo Git serialization.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:31-55 builds five production NewRunner(Config{}) instances and labels directive-file paths as model names under the obsolete script route. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:73-89 then calls ExecuteBeadWithConfig concurrently with those production runners. The current service-backed runner resolves the request to Codex, so each directive path is passed to codex exec as -m instead of being consumed by a hermetic script fixture. The test comments at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_concurrent_predispatch_test.go:35-37 explicitly say agent output is irrelevant. The package previously had to be repaired for the same 600-second budget under ddx-1a0d4d26, but this fixture has regressed into live provider execution.

PROPOSED FIX
- Replace the five production runners in this Git-lock regression with an explicit bounded hermetic AgentRunner fixture that returns the minimal no-changes result needed to reach and validate pre-dispatch serialization.
- Preserve the real temporary Git repository, five concurrent ExecuteBeadWithConfig calls, tracker commits, worktree creation, and HEAD CAS assertions.
- Add a provider-spawn tripwire: real/fake codex, claude, gemini, and provider-launch lookup must fail the test immediately if invoked.
- Audit adjacent direct NewRunner plus Harness=script fixtures reached by the normal internal/agent package gate and migrate any that can invoke live providers to the same hermetic boundary.
- Ensure subprocesses are canceled and reaped on test failure or timeout.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken production provider discovery, reduce the concurrency below five, delete the HEAD race assertions, or skip the test. Live provider integration remains build-tagged/explicit integration coverage, not part of the default package gate.

PARENT
None; root regression bead.

DEPS
None.

Add a spec-honesty check to lefthook.yml modeled on the existing evidence-lint/runtime-lint stanzas: run `go run ./tools/lint/spechonesty` over the docs/helix corpus (features/ plus the five 02-design subdirectories), scoped to staged doc changes in pre-commit, and add a full-tree gate in the ci block (mirroring the pattern near lefthook.yml:494-536). 3. rg -n "github.com/easel/fizeau.*(replace|=>)|github.com/easel/fizeau v0\\.0\\.0-" cli/go.mod cli/go.sum go.work go.work.sum returns no local replacement or pseudo-version.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx consumers need proof that Fizeau v0.15 Execute cancellation does not return while wrapped child or grandchild processes are still alive. Without a focused conformance test, downstream cleanup and lifecycle consumers can incorrectly assume process-tree containment from implementation details instead of the released public Fizeau contract.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/go.mod:5-8 pins github.com/easel/fizeau v0.14.50 and cli/go.sum:88-89 locks that version. cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:196-216 builds the public Execute request, while cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:283-367 consumes final events without proving cancellation waits for wrapped process-tree exit. cli/internal/agent/serviceconfig.go:17-48 is the sole production Fizeau constructor seam and should remain a seam rather than a place for DDx-specific process containment policy. docs/helix/06-iterate/phase1-lower-the-altitude-plan-2026-07-13.md:126-146 requires released public-boundary conformance before WB-1 consumers proceed.

PROPOSED FIX
After fizeau#fizeau-b9a2037c publishes immutable v0.15.0, ensure cli/go.mod and cli/go.sum use github.com/easel/fizeau v0.15.0 exactly if a sibling child has not already landed that pin. Add cli/internal/agent/fizeau_v015_cancellation_contract_test.go using only exported Fizeau APIs. The test must launch a wrapped process that spawns a child or grandchild, cancel Execute, and assert Execute returns only after both PIDs are gone.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement DDx retry, escalation, close, or review policy; adopt Docker portable runtime; delete DDx cleanup shims; add route catalogs or provider probes; select a concrete harness/model/provider; or use Fizeau cost, billing, or route evidence as an execution-policy input. Downstream beads own production consumers after this prerequisite closes. Do not add terminal-cost or portable-plan conformance beyond what is necessary for compilation.

PARENT
ddx-b8cacbeb.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
docs/helix/06-iterate/phase1-lower-the-altitude-plan-2026-07-13.md:126-146 and adr:ADR-024.

DEPS
External blocker fizeau#fizeau-b9a2037c must publish v0.15.0 with public typed terminal fields, absent/zero/positive cost presence, wrapped-process-tree containment, and opaque route-neutral portable runtime planning.

Wire it into pre-commit without mutating documents.

NON-SCOPE
Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete.

ddx-2e992616.

None for the linter; later status-restamp beads depend on this child.

- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` historically lacked outcome metadata that lets telemetry classify hit, miss, and cold-start savings records consistently.

DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, parent `ddx-1436e204`, parent `ddx-5dda007b`, child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace hit and miss telemetry events", sibling child "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", sibling child "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", sibling child "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation", child "attempt-backend: calculate reusable workspace savings estimates from allocation outcomes", child "attempt-backend: emit zero reusable workspace savings for cold-start attempts", child "attempt-backend: carry reusable workspace savings through execution telemetry", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace savings for reused attempts", and child "attempt-backend: combine workspace hit miss and savings telemetry". description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-b291b0f6 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
The mandatory `cd cli && go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./internal/agent` gate recursively launches the package test binary as DDx's hidden provider wrapper. During attempt `20260713T190502-df5adc46`, the parent `agent.test` spawned five concurrent `agent.test __provider-launch <real-provider>` helpers for more than three minutes, grew a 666 MB testlog, and left a real `codex --no-alt-screen` process reparented to the managed worker for 12 minutes at about 188 MiB RSS. This makes the package gate itself create the CPU/memory/orphan condition it is supposed to prevent.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:102-113` calls `os.Executable()` unconditionally and passes that path to `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH`.
- `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:152-163` repeats the same unconditional installation for the resolved-service path.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:83-118` writes each shim as `<ddxBinary> __provider-launch <realBinary>`. Under `go test`, `os.Executable()` is `agent.test`, not the DDx CLI and it has no Cobra `__provider-launch` dispatch. Re-executing it starts the test suite again; the recursive process can install shims and launch real providers that escape the original gate process group.
- `cli/cmd/provider_launch.go:25-68` is the actual hidden-command implementation, and exists only in the DDx CLI command graph.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce one injectable resolver for the provider-wrapper executable and use it from both service call sites. In package-test builds, install a suite-wide test resolver/guard that refuses to use the current `agent.test` executable as a provider wrapper while leaving direct `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH` tests free to supply an explicit real/fake DDx CLI binary. Fail closed with actionable evidence if a test fixture attempts to install a provider shim from a Go test binary. Preserve production PATH shim, `Pdeathsig`, process-group, and real CLI hidden-command behavior.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not remove provider parent-death protection in production.
- Do not replace Fizeau routing or provider discovery.
- Do not weaken the full `internal/agent` race gate or merely increase its timeout.
- Do not kill unrelated provider processes from other repositories.
- Scanner injection remains owned by `ddx-02200b1e`; fixture-specific spawn tripwires remain owned by `ddx-26bf19c7`.

PARENT AND DEPS

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can claim verification with a Verification mapping row whose evidence target is an inspectable runtime artifact path that does not exist. That lets a Complete stamp rely on unverifiable artifact names instead of current-revision evidence, and the analyzer currently reports nothing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no runtime-artifact existence check over parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
Wire the runtime artifact target resolver into the spechonesty analyzer run. For each Complete/Implemented document mapping row classified as an inspectable runtime artifact target, emit a missing-artifact diagnostic when the target does not resolve, naming the path exactly as written in the mapping row and identifying the requirement and source document. Rows that resolve pass artifact validation and emit nothing. Keep the analyzer read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that.

- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` exposes allocation outcome metadata, but tests do not prove reused-attempt savings are present in the same emitted event as slot allocation counts.
- Attempt-path savings counters are not summarized with hit/miss counters, so reuse wins can drift into a separate savings-only event without a regression failure.

PROPOSED FIX

Add focused regression coverage for the final emitted telemetry stream, asserting that reused-attempt savings are not emitted only through a separate savings-only event when the combined reusable workspace telemetry event is emitted.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT

acceptance:
1. `TestLocalCloneAttemptBackendReusesWorkerSlotAcrossSequentialAttempts` runs two sequential attempts and proves the second receives the same healthy slot while checking out its requested base revision.
2. `TestWorktreeAttemptBackendReusesWorkerSlotAcrossSequentialAttempts` proves the linked-worktree backend also reuses a healthy slot and resets it to the second attempt's requested base revision.
3. `TestReusableAttemptWorkspaceScrubsCrossBeadState` proves staged changes, modified tracked files, untracked files, evidence under `.ddx/executions/`, environment-derived credentials, and attempt cleanup metadata from bead A are absent from bead B.
4. `TestReusableAttemptWorkspaceQuarantinesDirtyOrLiveSlot` proves cleanup failure or a surviving descendant process prevents reuse, removes the slot from the pool, and emits operator-visible diagnostics.
5. `TestReusableAttemptWorkspaceRejectsRepositoryIdentityMismatch` proves a slot whose repository identity no longer matches the requesting project is not reused and a fresh workspace is created instead.
6. Successful cleanup returns a healthy slot to the pool for both backends rather than unconditionally running `WorktreeRemove`/`os.RemoveAll`, while existing `KeepOnError` and stale-worktree-registration recovery behaviour is preserved.
7. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run 'Test(LocalCloneAttemptBackendReusesWorkerSlotAcrossSequentialAttempts|WorktreeAttemptBackendReusesWorkerSlotAcrossSequentialAttempts|ReusableAttemptWorkspaceScrubsCrossBeadState|ReusableAttemptWorkspaceQuarantinesDirtyOrLiveSlot|ReusableAttemptWorkspaceRejectsRepositoryIdentityMismatch)' -count=1` passes.
8. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... ./internal/config/...` passes.
9. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes on the final staged tree.
description:
PROBLEM
Every bead attempt creates a fresh checkout and deletes it on cleanup, so identical sequential work on the same project pays full setup cost each time and discards all local state. Making a workspace survive between beads is only safe if DDx can prove the next bead sees exactly its requested base revision with no residue from the previous bead, and can refuse reuse when it cannot prove that.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:116-149` (`WorktreeAttemptBackend.Prepare`) creates a linked worktree at a fresh attempt-specific path via `gitOps.WorktreeAdd`, and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:182-190` (`WorktreeAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) unconditionally runs `WorktreeRemove`.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:199-233` (`LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Prepare`) runs a full `git clone` plus `checkout --detach` for every attempt, and `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:252-259` (`LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) deletes the whole clone with `os.RemoveAll`.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` (`ResolveAttemptBackend`) documents that local-clone is the sandbox-safe default, so the default path is the one paying full clone cost per bead.
- There is no reset/scrub path anywhere in `attempt_backend.go`: because the directory is always new, no code establishes that staged changes, modified tracked files, untracked files, evidence under `.ddx/executions/`, environment-derived credentials, or cleanup metadata written by `WriteExecutionCleanupMetadata` (`cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1019-1031`) are absent.

PROPOSED FIX
Build on the slot allocator from the sibling bead "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface" (DEPENDS ON that child; do not start until its allocator and config land). Teach both `WorktreeAttemptBackend.Prepare` and `LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Prepare` to request a slot, and when a healthy slot with a matching repository identity already exists, reset it to the requested base revision instead of recreating it: hard-reset tracked state, scrub staged and modified files, remove untracked files including evidence directories and attempt cleanup metadata, drop environment-derived credential material, and preserve only explicitly allowlisted paths. Verify repository identity before reuse and fall back to a fresh workspace on mismatch. On cleanup, return a healthy slot to the pool; on cleanup failure, surviving descendant processes, or a failed post-reset integrity check, quarantine the slot so it is never reused and emit operator-visible diagnostics. Preserve existing stale-worktree-registration recovery (`isStaleWorktreeRegistrationError`, `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:157-173`) and the existing `KeepOnError` behaviour.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not implement Rust/Cargo build-cache preservation or toolchain/lockfile invalidation (sibling child).
- Do not change `execute_bead.go` orchestration or add telemetry (sibling child).

description:
PROBLEM
While the managed DDx worker decomposed ddx-29491a0e on 2026-07-13, the preclaim-decompose Codex provider remained live for more than two minutes, but `ddx work status --json` changed to active_work.count=0 and reported no bead_id, phase, or last_activity_at. Operators therefore see an apparently idle worker while queue-critical model work is running.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1604-1617 constructs the sidecar liveness reporter but explicitly defers emission until a bead is claimed. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3108-3120 invokes PostAttemptDecompositionHook before claim without setting a resolving phase or ticking liveness.

PROPOSED FIX
Publish candidate-scoped resolving liveness before dispatching preclaim decomposition, heartbeat it while the provider runs, and include provider-child observations without creating a bead lease. The sidecar status must expose the candidate bead ID, phase=resolving, refreshed last_activity_at, and provider-child metadata before any claim or lease exists.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker.

PARENT
Split from root reliability regression bead: work: surface, bound, and reap preclaim decomposition lifecycle.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first so the internal/agent verification gate does not launch five real Codex providers.

description:
PROBLEM
Complete/Implemented documents can claim verification with a Verification mapping row whose evidence target is an inspectable runtime artifact path that does not exist. That lets a Complete stamp rely on unverifiable artifact names instead of current-revision evidence, and the analyzer currently reports nothing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The spechonesty analyzer path is absent in this checkout at cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/analyzer.go:1, and the analyzer run has no runtime-artifact existence check over parsed Verification rows. The governing contract is docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:67, requiring every Complete/Implemented mapping row to name an exact evidence target, and docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:68, requiring rejection of mappings to nonexistent artifacts. Current-revision executable verification is reinforced at docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md:176.

PROPOSED FIX
Extend the spechonesty analyzer runtime-artifact validation so each Complete/Implemented Verification mapping row classified as an inspectable runtime artifact target emits a missing-artifact diagnostic when the resolver cannot resolve the target. The diagnostic must name the artifact path exactly as written in the mapping row and must be emitted only for unresolved inspectable runtime artifact targets. Keep the analyzer read-only.

NON-SCOPE
Do not reimplement target classification or path resolution — consume the resolver child. Do not handle waivers — that is the waiver child. Do not parse requirement inventories or mapping tables — that is the mapping-parser child. Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Status parsing lives in the scaffold child. Duplicate-id and stale-observation detection are a sibling child. Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope. Do not enforce requirement coverage cardinality or duplicate mapping counts — the coverage-cardinality child owns that. Do not resolve Go Test* symbols or static check names — the evidence-target child owns those checks. Do not enforce command allowlisting — the verification-command allowlist child owns that.

DEPS: parent ddx-e743ce67; grandparent ddx-29449fa5; root dependency ddx-471d66b6; the spechonesty scaffold/status-parser child; the Verification mapping-parser child that provides the inventory + rows model; the runtime artifact target resolver child. GOVERNING ARTIFACT: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md WB-1 steps 3-4.

description:
PROBLEM
A reusable attempt workspace that fails cleanup or still has descendant processes after an attempt is unsafe to return to the healthy pool. DDx needs a refusal path that quarantines that slot and surfaces operator-visible diagnostics.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:182-190` (`WorktreeAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) currently removes linked-worktree workspaces rather than tracking reusable slot health, quarantine state, or reuse eligibility.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:252-259` (`LocalCloneAttemptBackend.Cleanup`) currently removes local-clone workspaces rather than tracking reusable slot health, quarantine state, or reuse eligibility.
- There is no reusable-slot descendant-process refusal path in `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go`, so live processes would otherwise be indistinguishable from a clean reusable slot.

PROPOSED FIX
During cleanup for both attempt backends, detect cleanup failures and surviving descendant processes. Mark the affected reusable slot quarantined, remove it from the healthy reusable pool, and emit operator-visible diagnostics containing slot, backend, project, and quarantine reason. A quarantined slot must never be reused by later attempts.

GOVERNING ARTIFACTS
Parent bead: `ddx-388ca2af`. Depends on sibling allocator/config child: `attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface`.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this child concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not implement Rust/Cargo build-cache preservation or toolchain/lockfile invalidation.
- Do not change `execute_bead.go` orchestration or add telemetry.
- Do not implement repository identity mismatch or post-reset integrity quarantine behavior except as minimal fixtures needed for cleanup/live-process coverage.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-53df5e2f requires post-migration verification that reads migrated beads back from Axon/Postgres and detects field-level drift. Drift detection should be independently executable from clean round-trip fixture expansion, dry-run behavior, write-path apply mechanics, and CLI routing.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The importer exposes MigrateAxonOptions.Verify at cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:38 and calls verifyImportedAxonCorpus from cli/internal/bead/import_postgres.go:113 after writes. If verifyImportedAxonCorpus or its comparison helpers are absent or shallow, ddx bead migrate --to-axon --verify can report success even when stored Axon data differs from the JSONL source corpus.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement or complete verifyImportedAxonCorpus and supporting comparison helpers so verification reads back the imported Axon target corpus, compares migrated source beads field-for-field, and returns an error that names the affected bead ID and the drifted field when target data is changed post-import. Keep implementation compatible with existing sample-based verification if a corpus-size threshold already exists; otherwise compare the bounded imported set produced by --limit or the full import.

NON-SCOPE
- Schema-versioning migration ladder; deferred until first v1-to-v2 breaking change.
- Real-wire integration test against actual Postgres; separate WIRE bead.
- Continuous sync between JSONL and Postgres.
- CLI flag parsing beyond consuming the Verify option; sibling child owns command UX.
- Core apply/idempotency mechanics except as needed to create verifier fixtures; sibling child owns apply path.
- Dry-run counting/no-mutation semantics; sibling child owns dry-run behavior.
- Clean round-trip fixture breadth for attachment/extras preservation; sibling child owns that proof.
- Do not claim or edit parent bead ddx-53df5e2f tracker data manually; tracker mutations must go through ddx bead commands.

GOVERNING CONTEXT

description:
PROBLEM
Production execute-bead orchestration still prepares a fresh throwaway workspace for each attempt, so the reusable slot pool implemented by sibling work is not used by real linked-worktree or local-clone executions.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` calls `attemptBackend.Prepare(...)` directly for every attempt and treats the returned workspace as a disposable per-attempt workspace.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` (`ResolveAttemptBackend`) constructs attempt backends without threading a reusable-workspace policy, slot pool handle, or worker-slot identity into the linked-worktree and local-clone implementations.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af` and the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". Thread the resolved reusable-workspace policy and worker-slot identity through `ResolveAttemptBackend` into the linked-worktree and local-clone backends. Make production preparation use the bounded slot allocator when reuse is enabled. Keep the existing per-attempt workspace path when reuse is disabled.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.

description:

The execution prompt at cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2046 documents blocked prose but no typed local-resource contract.

description:
PROBLEM
Reused attempts must report slot hit count and the associated time-saved and bytes-saved values in the same telemetry event as cold-start attempts. Without this, operators must correlate separate hit/miss and savings signals to compare reuse outcomes.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares reusable workspaces and performs cleanup but does not emit one combined telemetry record that includes both reuse hit counts and savings values.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` exposes outcome metadata that can identify reusable workspace allocation results, but reused-attempt savings are not carried into the same emitted event as slot allocation counts.
- Attempt-path savings counters are not summarized with hit/miss counters, so reuse wins cannot be observed from one event.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, parent `ddx-1436e204`, parent `ddx-5dda007b`, child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace hit and miss telemetry events", sibling child "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", sibling child "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", sibling child "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation", child "attempt-backend: calculate reusable workspace savings estimates from allocation outcomes", child "attempt-backend: emit zero reusable workspace savings for cold-start attempts", child "attempt-backend: carry reusable workspace savings through execution telemetry", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace savings for reused attempts", child "attempt-backend: define combined reusable workspace telemetry payload", and child "attempt-backend: emit combined reusable workspace telemetry for cold starts". Wire reused allocation outcomes through the combined telemetry payload so every reused attempt emits slot hit information plus the time-saved and bytes-saved values supplied by the allocation/execution savings contract. Ensure the final event stream uses one shape for reuse and cold-start attempts.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Parent bead `ddx-54ff73df`: attempt-backend combined workspace hit, miss, and savings telemetry.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.
- Do not alter the estimate formula except as needed to consume the contract delivered by the savings-estimate child.
- Do not change the existing Docker attempt backend shared-cache behaviour while adding this event.

description:
PROBLEM
Operators cannot tell whether reusable attempt workspaces are being used because execute-bead preparation and cleanup do not emit hit, miss, or cold-start observability events for reusable workspace slots.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares and cleans up workspaces without emitting reuse-specific observability events.
- No hit/miss counters exist in the attempt path, leaving no signal for slot reuse behavior.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, the child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", and the sibling children "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", and "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation". Emit reusable workspace hit, miss, and cold-start counts through the existing execution event/observability path from execute-bead orchestration. Scope events by project identity, worker-slot identity, resolved backend policy, and attempt identity for both reuse and cold-start attempts.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.

description:
PROBLEM
After the ddx-29491a0e preclaim decomposer returned on 2026-07-13, an interactive nested `codex --no-alt-screen` process (PID 607041, process group 607041) remained directly under the DDx worker until the operator terminated it. Preclaim providers can therefore leak CPU after successful fallback or other hook exits.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3108-3120 invokes PostAttemptDecompositionHook before claim without wrapping the hook in provider-descendant cleanup. Attempt-end descendant reaping in cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1150-1163 is never reached because decomposition happens before an implementation attempt exists.

PROPOSED FIX
Establish a preclaim lifecycle process baseline immediately before invoking the decomposition hook and reap every provider descendant introduced by the hook on success, deterministic fallback, error, timeout, and cancellation. Preserve any provider process present in the pre-hook baseline and any process owned by another worker.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker.

PARENT
Split from root reliability regression bead: work: surface, bound, and reap preclaim decomposition lifecycle.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first so the internal/agent verification gate does not launch five real Codex providers.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-24949caf is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 2 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM: Restarting the DDx user service during active supervised work can hang until systemd times out, leaving systemd to SIGKILL server child processes. Live evidence from 2026-07-07 03:05:19 EDT: `ddx server stop` did not return until systemd marked `ddx-server.service` failed with `Result: timeout` and killed leftover git subprocesses, interrupting the Axon worker attempt that was in post-execution handling.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE: `cli/internal/server/server.go:379-385` cancels the supervisor and then waits on `supervisorDone` with no timeout. Worker cleanup is only reached afterward at `cli/internal/server/server.go:388-395`. The worker shutdown path itself has a bounded wait (`cli/internal/server/workers.go:1696-1703`), but it is unreachable while the supervisor goroutine is stuck in a reconcile/git operation. The installed systemd unit generated from `cli/cmd/server_service.go:26-42` has no explicit stop timeout or ExecStop mitigation, so the default systemd timeout eventually kills the whole cgroup.

PROPOSED FIX: Make server shutdown bounded and ordered so worker cleanup always runs promptly even when supervisor reconciliation is slow or stuck. A good implementation is to cancel the supervisor, wait only a short bounded grace for `supervisorDone`, continue to `supervisorRegistry.Shutdown()` / `workers.Shutdown()` on timeout, and surface/log the supervisor timeout without preventing worker cleanup.

NON-SCOPE: Do not rewrite worker execution semantics, change bead claim/lease policy, or alter unrelated service install behavior.

Parent: none. Dependencies: none.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- Add or update a worker-manager shutdown regression so a live managed worker with descendant git/provider subprocesses is reaped through the existing worker shutdown path even when supervisor cancellation is slow.
- `Server.Shutdown()` must not block indefinitely on `supervisorDone`; timeout behavior must return/log a useful error while continuing to close bead hub and stop land coordinators.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
DDx still installs provider-binary PATH shims, exposes a hidden provider-launch wrapper, scans concrete harness process trees, and signals/reaps Fizeau-owned children. Fizeau v0.15 containment work is implemented upstream but not yet published or pinned, so DDx cannot yet delete the safety fallback. Without a dedicated consumer bead, publishing v0.15 would leave this forbidden boundary crossing in DDx indefinitely.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:93-102,116-128,276-297 installs the provider shim and performs route-aware child cleanup around Fizeau Execute.
- cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:13-56 and 100-179 defines the hidden wrapper contract and concrete provider binary shims.
- cli/cmd/provider_launch.go:12-70 plus provider_launch platform files exposes the direct provider exec boundary.
- cli/internal/agent/provider_children.go:21-40,92-240,242-478 discovers, classifies, signals, and reaps provider children using concrete route/harness facts.
- cli/internal/agent/orphan_harness_reaper.go:42-169 plus orphan_harness_reaper_linux.go:22-113 discovers and kills orphan harness processes.
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1249-1258 and execute_bead_loop.go:1616-1618 retain attempt-end and liveness integration.
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_process.go:61-195 and cli/internal/server/workers_reap_unix.go:33-213 mix Fizeau-owned descendants into otherwise DDx-owned attempt/worker cleanup.
- Fizeau containment epic fizeau-c795e7d9 is closed, but release bead fizeau-b9a2037c must publish and prove cancellation/caller-death cleanup before DDx removes the fallback.

PROPOSED FIX
After pinning the compatible Fizeau release, add consumer conformance proving Execute cancellation and caller death terminate every wrapped harness/provider process tree. Delete the PATH shim, hidden provider-launch command/platform implementation, concrete provider binary list, provider-child/orphan-harness census and reapers, route-aware child liveness, attempt-end provider reap, and provider-descendant branches in generic cleanup. DDx retains only cancellation of the context supplied to Fizeau Execute and may supervise/reap DDx-owned worker, attempt, verification, and container processes. No concrete returned route fact may authorize a signal.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken DDx-owned worker/attempt/container cleanup, move bead/worktree/verification/landing ownership to Fizeau, parse terminal text, or implement the typed outcome adapter owned by ddx-66a8883f.

PARENT
ddx-b8cacbeb.

DEPS
fizeau#fizeau-b9a2037c publishes the process-tree containment contract and is the structured external blocker. fizeau#fizeau-c795e7d9 supplies the already-landed implementation.
notes: Fizeau v0.15 pin and public conformance are centralized in ddx-00d406ce; this consumer must not repin Fizeau independently.

description:
PROBLEM
Existing agent tests intentionally create corrupted Git configuration to prove execute-bead repair behavior, but those fixtures must never mutate the real repository running the tests. The two affected tests must keep their intended assertions while operating only inside dedicated fixture repositories.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_stay_alive_test.go:1244-1286 deliberately sets `core.bare=true` in a script-harness fixture. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_env_isolation_test.go:181-237 asserts a separate contamination case does not affect the primary checkout. The observed full-hook run of `go test -short -race ./internal/agent` nevertheless rewrote `/home/erik/Projects/ddx/.git/config` at 2026-07-17 09:41 with `core.bare=true` and test user values, which means these fixture paths can still reach shared config outside their intended sandbox.

PROPOSED FIX
Refactor TestExecuteBeadWorkerCannotMutatePrimaryGitConfig and TestWorkRepairsCoreBareAndContinuesSameCandidate setup to create and use dedicated temporary repositories/config scopes for all intentional Git corruption and repair assertions. Snapshot the invoking repository configuration before fixture execution where practical, assert the fixture repository still observes and repairs its own `core.bare=true` state, and make the tests fail during setup if they cannot prove they are targeting private fixture config.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken the existing core.bare/core.worktree repair behavior, remove execute-bead config isolation, alter user project Git configuration, or change DDx/Fizeau routing. This child only changes the existing core.bare repair/contamination fixtures and their focused assertions; stale index-lock recovery is ddx-3f156500 and main-git lock safety is ddx-1c8d9319. Parent bead: ddx-8b22914e. Deps: none; independent defect discovered while validating ddx-3f156500.

acceptance:
1. TestExecuteBeadLoop_RepeatedBestEffortReadinessErrorsDoNotStopDrain creates more than DefaultPreClaimWarnRepeatThreshold ready beads whose pre-claim hook returns the same nonfatal intake error; it proves all beads execute/close, Run has no terminal OperatorAttention, and a durable non-terminal operator-attention event is emitted exactly once.
2. TestPreClaimWarnSameFingerprintEscalatesAfterThreshold or its successor still proves a claim-blocking system_unready policy stops before the threshold bead.
3. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -run "Test(ExecuteBeadLoop_RepeatedBestEffortReadinessErrorsDoNotStopDrain|PreClaimWarnSameFingerprintEscalatesAfterThreshold)" -count=1 passes.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s passes.
5. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
A DDx watch worker exits after five distinct beads when the best-effort readiness hook repeatedly returns system_unready, even though each failure is explicitly logged as continuing and the worker can still claim and execute beads. This converts an advisory Fizeau readiness outage into a queue-wide drain stop.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3010-3058 logs intakeErr as "check unavailable ... (continuing)" but passes it to appendPreClaimWarn. execute_bead_loop.go:1961-1984 makes the fifth matching warning set OperatorAttention and terminate Run. The observed watch run exited after ddx-029c1dde, ddx-744b0996, ddx-b0de0d36, and ddx-8c8675ba with preclaim_warn_repeated while all failures were non-blocking readiness-route JSON errors.

PROPOSED FIX
For fail-open best-effort readiness intake errors, retain durable warning/operator-attention observability but do not return Stop from watch/drain execution. Keep terminal behavior for claim-blocking readiness policy, project corruption, and other genuine safety stops. Add focused regression proof using a repeated intakeErr across more than DefaultPreClaimWarnRepeatThreshold beads that confirms the worker completes the available queue and records non-terminal attention.

NON-SCOPE
Do not change Fizeau routing, harness selection, failure-class vocabulary, readiness policy when configured blocking, or bead execution escalation.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-b291b0f6 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 3 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
The mandatory `cd cli && go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./internal/agent` gate recursively launches the package test binary as DDx's hidden provider wrapper. During attempt `20260713T190502-df5adc46`, the parent `agent.test` spawned five concurrent `agent.test __provider-launch <real-provider>` helpers for more than three minutes, grew a 666 MB testlog, and left a real `codex --no-alt-screen` process reparented to the managed worker for 12 minutes at about 188 MiB RSS. This makes the package gate itself create the CPU/memory/orphan condition it is supposed to prevent.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/agent_runner_service.go:102-113` calls `os.Executable()` unconditionally and passes that path to `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH`.
- `cli/internal/agent/service_run.go:152-163` repeats the same unconditional installation for the resolved-service path.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_spawn.go:83-118` writes each shim as `<ddxBinary> __provider-launch <realBinary>`. Under `go test`, `os.Executable()` is `agent.test`, not the DDx CLI and it has no Cobra `__provider-launch` dispatch. Re-executing it starts the test suite again; the recursive process can install shims and launch real providers that escape the original gate process group.
- `cli/cmd/provider_launch.go:25-68` is the actual hidden-command implementation, and exists only in the DDx CLI command graph.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce one injectable resolver for the provider-wrapper executable and use it from both service call sites. In package-test builds, install a suite-wide test resolver/guard that refuses to use the current `agent.test` executable as a provider wrapper while leaving direct `EnsureProviderShimOnPATH` tests free to supply an explicit real/fake DDx CLI binary. Fail closed with actionable evidence if a test fixture attempts to install a provider shim from a Go test binary. Preserve production PATH shim, `Pdeathsig`, process-group, and real CLI hidden-command behavior.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not remove provider parent-death protection in production.
- Do not replace Fizeau routing or provider discovery.
- Do not weaken the full `internal/agent` race gate or merely increase its timeout.
- Do not kill unrelated provider processes from other repositories.
- Scanner injection remains owned by `ddx-02200b1e`; fixture-specific spawn tripwires remain owned by `ddx-26bf19c7`.

PARENT AND DEPS
...[truncated]

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent -run "^(TestProviderShimExecutableResolver_RejectsGoTestBinary|TestRunAgentViaService_UsesProviderShimExecutableResolver|TestDispatchViaResolvedConfig_UsesProviderShimExecutableResolver|TestAgentPackageSuite_DoesNotExecTestBinaryAsProviderLauncher|TestExecutor_ProviderSpawnSetsPdeathsigAndSetpgid)$" -count=1 -timeout 120s` passes.
- `cd cli && go test -short -race -timeout 30m ./internal/agent` passes without any `agent.test __provider-launch` descendant, orphaned real provider, or recursive package-test process.
- `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.

description:
PROBLEM
Once preclaim decomposition starts publishing resolving liveness, stale candidate state could make `ddx work status --json` report old bead IDs or phases after the hook exits. The existing loop.start structured event ordering must also remain stable so downstream execution telemetry does not regress.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1604-1617 defers liveness emission until claim, so there is currently no preclaim transient state lifecycle to clear. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:3108-3120 invokes PostAttemptDecompositionHook before claim, so adding liveness there can accidentally emit before the existing loop.start event unless the new lifecycle is sequenced explicitly.

PROPOSED FIX
Clear transient candidate resolving state on every preclaim decomposition exit, including success, deterministic fallback/error, timeout, and cancellation. Sequence the new preclaim liveness setup so the existing loop.start structured event remains the first structured event while still allowing resolving liveness before claim.

NON-SCOPE
Do not claim the parent before decomposition, change decomposition prompts or AC-map validation, change queue ordering, or make preclaim model work count as an implementation attempt. Do not kill provider processes that predate the hook baseline or belong to another worker.

PARENT
Split from root reliability regression bead: work: surface, bound, and reap preclaim decomposition lifecycle.

DEPS
ddx-aa6cc320 must land first so the internal/agent verification gate does not launch five real Codex providers.

description:
PROBLEM
A ddx work worker can spend minutes synchronously measuring and deleting one accumulated scratch tree before it claims useful work. During the 2026-07-13 niflheim incident, one cleanup pass performed hundreds of megabytes of physical reads; the same path timed out at both 120 seconds in isolation and 600 seconds in the full package gate. This creates unbounded CPU/I/O latency and makes queue progress inversely proportional to stale cache size.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go:1687 runs the execution cleanup pass on the claim path. cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:620-747 scans every matching scratch directory, calls measureTreeWithContext over an unbounded tree, and then calls os.RemoveAll, which walks the tree again and cannot observe context cancellation. cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:830-843 includes the shared cache parent and legacy process temp directory by default. A large stale directory therefore monopolizes the single queue worker with no per-pass item, inode, byte, or wall-clock budget.

PROPOSED FIX
- Put a deterministic wall-clock/work budget around scratch discovery, measurement, and reclamation on worker passes.
- Make cancellation effective during both measurement and deletion; do not enter an uninterruptible whole-tree RemoveAll after the budget expires.
- Persist or rediscover unfinished candidates safely so later passes continue reclamation without restarting an O(tree) measurement from zero.
- Return a non-fatal structured deferred-cleanup observation when the budget is exhausted, then allow candidate selection to proceed.
- Preserve liveness, ownership, registered-worktree, and minimum-age checks before any mutation.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_loop.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop.go only as needed for the bounded pass contract
- focused cleanup tests

NON-SCOPE
Do not delete live worktrees, reduce the six-hour minimum age, disable cleanup, or treat cleanup deferral as bead failure.

PARENT
None; root production reliability regression.

DEPS
Depends on ddx-e6abf4a6 so the hermetic test boundary lands before production cleanup stress tests run.

PROBLEM
The embedded-dispatch runner tests currently create isolated HOME directories with os.MkdirTemp and then change HOME. On Niflheim, an abandoned ddx-home-* directory accumulated a large private Go module cache, and later test gates recursively traversed that scratch tree. The gap is not just fixture cleanup; there is no regression test proving the isolated HOME stays free of go/pkg/mod and does not mint a fresh process-global ddx-home-* under os.TempDir.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:29-34 and cli/internal/agent/runner_test.go:56-61 create the raw HOME fixture and discard cleanup errors, which makes it possible for Go subprocess defaults to spill into the temp tree and for abandoned ddx-home-* directories to persist undetected.

Add tripwire tests in the runner test file that exercise both embedded-dispatch paths, snapshot os.TempDir before and after the fixture, and prove no new ddx-home-* directory is created. Also assert the isolated HOME never gains go/pkg/mod. These tests should fail if the fixture pattern regresses.

PROBLEM
The reusable production preparation path must remain opt-in. Operators who disable workspace reuse in configuration still need the existing disposable per-attempt workspace creation and destructive cleanup behaviour.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` currently has only the disposable per-attempt preparation path, and the reusable-slot integration must not remove that fallback.
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` resolves attempt backends without an explicit reusable-workspace policy boundary, so disabled configuration needs a regression test once the policy is threaded into backend construction.

PROPOSED FIX

Keep the existing per-attempt workspace path when reuse is disabled by configuration. Ensure disabled mode does not acquire a slot, does not reuse the previous linked-worktree/local-clone workspace, and still performs the current destructive cleanup for disposable workspaces.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.

2. The skip records an auditable note/event on the affected bead naming the open dep ID; asserted within `TestRollUpClose_RefusesBeadWithOpenBlocksDep`.
3. Roll-up still auto-closes eligible beads whose blocking deps are all closed (no regression to RC-2/RC-3 covered by existing TestClose_EpicAutoClose_* / TestClose_WalkUp_* / TestClose_SupersededCascade_Eligible); covered by new `TestRollUpClose_AllowsBeadWithClosedBlocksDep`.

description:
PROBLEM: The 2026-07-06 pqueue incident: a server-managed worker performed a tracker-only roll-up close (no closing commit) on pqueue-842ac11f while it still carried an open 'blocks' dependency on pqueue-657e5f8d (in_progress). The programmatic auto-close paths do not validate dependency status, so a parent/superseded bead is auto-closed even when it has unmet blocking deps.

ROOT CAUSE: `Store.cascadeAndWalkUp` (cli/internal/bead/store.go:1661) runs auto-close paths that call `SetLifecycleStatus(..., StatusClosed, ...)` directly, bypassing dependency checks: (a) RC-2 cascade-close of superseded beads via `cascadeCloseSuperseeded` (store.go:1833), guarded only by `canCascadeCloseSuperseeded` (store.go:1867) which checks supersession/claim state but not deps; (b) RC-3 walk-up via `walkUpClosureCandidate` (store.go:1712) which auto-closes dead-intermediate (`execution-eligible==false`) and epic parents once children are terminal. Neither consults sibling dependency statuses. This is the exact path that produced the incident (tracker-only roll-up, no commit). Reconcile also closes programmatically at cli/internal/bead/reconcile.go:285 — out of scope here.

PROPOSED FIX: Depends on the sibling bead adding `ErrDependencyGateRejected` and `Store.UnclosedBlockingDeps(id)` (cli/internal/bead/errors.go, store.go). Before each auto-close `SetLifecycleStatus(x.ID, StatusClosed, ...)` in `cascadeCloseSuperseeded` (store.go:1833) and before the closed transition inside `walkUpClosureCandidate` (store.go:1712), call `s.UnclosedBlockingDeps(<candidateID>)`; if it returns a non-empty slice, SKIP that auto-close (leave the bead open), append an audit note/event naming the open dep IDs (mirroring `appendClosureRejectNote`, store.go:2079), and continue the walk without closing that node. The roll-up must not abort the whole operation — it selectively skips the ineligible bead. If the sibling primitive has not landed, add a minimal resolver inline at the roll-up call sites rather than duplicating the exported method.

NON-SCOPE: Do NOT change `Store.Close` / `Store.CloseWithEvidence` / `Store.UpdateWithLifecycleStatus` direct-close gating (sibling bead). Do NOT change claim paths (sibling bead). Do NOT change `Reconcile` (reconcile.go:285). Do NOT alter epic/dead-intermediate terminal-child counting beyond adding the dep-gate skip.

description:
PROBLEM
Commit `020853315` added `ListModelsWithProbeContainment`, which fixes the immediate leaked-probe symptom but identifies ownership by taking a process-wide provider baseline and reaping every provider descendant that appears afterward. A concurrent legitimate provider started under the same worker after the baseline can therefore be killed as if it belonged to this discovery call. Both scans use `context.Background()`, each termination can wait independently, and cleanup scan/termination errors are discarded, so the containment path can itself wedge or report false success.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/model_discovery_containment.go:28-35` attributes all post-baseline provider descendants to one `ListModels` call without a call-owned process/session identity.
- `cli/internal/agent/model_discovery_containment.go:38-64` runs both baseline and cleanup through `context.Background()` and drops cleanup errors.
- `cli/internal/agent/provider_children_unix.go:18-58` enumerates the host through `ps` and flattens descendants without PPID, process-group, session, or launch-owner metadata needed to prove call ownership.

PROPOSED FIX
Use an exact call-owned provider/session handle from the Fizeau cancellation work in `ddx-a751a7b1` when available and remove the process-wide baseline sweep. If a local fallback is still required, retain ancestry/session/launch ownership, serialize ambiguous lifecycle discovery, bound baseline and cleanup enumeration with explicit deadlines, fail closed by preserving ambiguous processes, and surface cleanup failures in the returned error and execution evidence. Cleanup must never wait on `context.Background()` or kill a provider solely because it appeared after a PID snapshot.

NON-SCOPE
Do not disable model discovery, extend the caller timeout, kill manual provider sessions, kill active implementation harnesses or their fixtures, weaken attempt-end cleanup, or change route selection.

PARENT
`ddx-f84ee9a7` (Niflheim provider-test CPU incident).

DEPS
Related to `ddx-a751a7b1` for the preferred upstream call-owned cancellation handle and `ddx-44e89575` for provider ancestry ownership; no hard dependency so the bounded fail-closed fallback can land independently.

description:
PROBLEM
There is no mechanical way to read a DDx document's status stamp, so downstream verification-coverage, duplicate-id, and stale-observation checks have nothing to build on. Status markers are heterogeneous: some docs use a body line `**Status:**` with free-text qualifiers, some use YAML frontmatter `status:`, and 40 of 56 design docs (including SD-013 and TD-027) have no status marker at all.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
The package `cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/` does not exist. The intended pattern is the sibling analyzer at cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/analyzer.go with a CLI entrypoint at cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/cmd/evidencelint/main.go and testdata fixtures under cli/tools/lint/evidencelint/testdata/. The mechanical contract is defined in docs/helix/06-iterate/phase2-doc-truth-plan-2026-07-13.md under WB-1, steps 1-2.

PROPOSED FIX
Create `cli/tools/lint/spechonesty/` (analyzer.go, analyzer_test.go, cmd/spechonesty/main.go, testdata/ fixtures) modeled on evidencelint. Implement a status parser that (a) recognizes both encodings — a body `**Status:**` line and YAML frontmatter `status:` — and normalizes free-text qualifiers to a base status (e.g. `Complete`, `Implemented`, `Proposed`, `In Progress`, `Deferred`, `Aspirational`), and (b) treats a missing status on any SD/TD/ADR document as a lint failure requiring a stamp. This missing-status rule — not the Complete-check — is what catches SD-013 and TD-027. Parsing must be deterministic and read-only; the linter never mutates documents.

NON-SCOPE
Do not auto-restamp documents, infer proof from prose, fetch network state, or mark aspirational metrics complete. Do not implement verification-coverage, waiver, duplicate-id, or stale-observation logic here (later children). Prose quality and AC numbering style are out of scope.

PARENT: ddx-2e992616. DEPS: none — this child lands first as the package foundation; later children depend on it.

description:
<context-digest>
<principles>Spec-first development · Executable specifications · Audit trail required · Work is a DAG · Drift is debt · Inspect and adapt</principles>
<concerns>go-std | security-owasp | testing</concerns>
<practices>Go domain interface with contract tests against real implementations · project-scoped durable files · no call-recording mocks · go test + lefthook</practices>
<adrs>ADR-022 rev 6 requires one reconnecting coordination client, durable ordered offline journal, idempotency keys, and a cross-process offline project lock.</adrs>
<governing>FEAT-006 Worker Contract: connected mutations use the server; disconnected manual workers apply the same operations locally and reconcile before new online writes.</governing>
</context-digest>

PROBLEM
Disconnected/manual worker mutations have no durable append record API, so a process crash can lose sequence ordering, idempotency keys, payload hashes, preconditions, or outcomes required for later reconciliation before online writes.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/workerprobe/probe.go:129-224 buffers only workerprobe events in memory. cli/cmd/try.go:256-259 and cli/cmd/execute_loop_shared.go:280-282 construct local landing coordination directly, so no package-level production API records idempotency-keyed offline coordination mutations durably before local execution proceeds.

Add a project-scoped offline journal package under cli/internal/agent that can create/open a durable journal file, append mutation records with monotonic sequence numbers, idempotency key, payload hash, precondition, and outcome fields, and close/reopen without losing the next sequence number. description:
PROBLEM
The normal internal/agent unit-test gate reads and deletes host-global DDx scratch trees. On 2026-07-13, TestWorkCleanup_RunsAfterSetupFailureBeforeNextClaim drove about 431 MB of physical reads, timed out after 120 seconds in isolation, and caused the required 600-second package gate to time out. This makes test duration depend on accumulated host cache state and adds substantial I/O/CPU pressure while ddx work is trying to drain the queue.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_cleanup_test.go:269-288 creates a production NewExecutionCleanupManager for t.TempDir but does not override TempRoot or ScratchRoots. cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:830-843 therefore derives the shared cache parent and legacy process temp directory. Cleanup reaches cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup.go:620-747, where it recursively measures and removes every old matching scratch directory. The timeout stack was in measureTreeWithContext from cleanupScratchRoots, not in the predispatch fixture under test.

PROPOSED FIX
- Give every execution-cleanup unit fixture an explicit hermetic TempRoot and ScratchRoots beneath its own t.TempDir before calling Cleanup.
- Add a shared test helper if needed so future fixtures cannot silently fall back to ~/.cache/ddx or the process temp root.
- Add a sentinel/tripwire proving the loop-cleanup test cannot enumerate, measure, or remove a scratch root outside its fixture root.
- Audit adjacent NewExecutionCleanupManager test call sites reached by ./internal/agent and apply the same boundary where they invoke Cleanup.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_loop_cleanup_test.go
- cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_test.go and nearest cleanup test helpers as required

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken production cleanup, change retention policy, or skip cleanup assertions. Production cleanup latency is tracked separately.

PARENT
None; root gate-reliability regression.

DEPS
None.

acceptance:
1. TestTrackerLockRuntimePathsIgnoredWithoutGitignore proves the guard sidecar path is excluded from synthesizeCommitExcludePathspecs, ignored by preDispatchCheckpointIgnoredPath, and ignored by checkoutSyncDeferralIgnoredPath even when .gitignore has no applicable rule, while an ordinary untracked implementation file remains visible to all three.
2. All three surfaces reference the shared package-local sidecar path helper/constant rather than an independently duplicated literal (asserted structurally in TestTrackerLockRuntimePathsIgnoredWithoutGitignore).
3. cd cli && go test -race ./internal/agent/... -run "TestTrackerLockRuntimePathsIgnoredWithoutGitignore" -count=20 passes.
4. cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s passes.
5. lefthook run pre-commit passes.
description:
PROBLEM
The never-deleted advisory-guard sidecar for the main-git lock is a permanent on-disk object. Unless every DDx surface that inspects the working tree ignores it independently of project .gitignore state, it becomes runtime dirt: staged by synthesized commits, flagged as pre-dispatch dirt, or blocking checkout sync.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/gitops_real.go:165-205 (synthesizeCommitExcludePathspecs) enumerates exclude pathspecs (currently including .ddx/.git-tracker.lock) but not the new guard sidecar. cli/internal/agent/predispatch_dirty.go:477-488 (preDispatchCheckpointIgnoredPath) matches .ddx/.git-tracker.lock and its children but not the sidecar. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_land.go:923-931 (checkoutSyncDeferralIgnoredPath) matches .ddx/.git-tracker.lock and its children but not the sidecar. Each must ignore the sidecar independently of whether .gitignore has an applicable rule.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Phase 0 WB-5 single-winner cross-process stale-break protocol: docs/helix/06-iterate/phase0-stop-the-self-harm-plan-2026-07-13.md:124-132.

PROPOSED FIX
Using the package-local guard sidecar path helper/constant introduced by the guard-primitive child (do not hardcode the literal in three places), extend all three surfaces to exclude/ignore the sidecar path: add an exclude pathspec in synthesizeCommitExcludePathspecs, add a case in preDispatchCheckpointIgnoredPath, and add a clause in checkoutSyncDeferralIgnoredPath. The sidecar must be ignored even when .gitignore contains no applicable rule (i.e. matching is code-level, not delegated to git check-ignore). Ordinary untracked implementation files must remain visible to all three surfaces.

NON-SCOPE
This child does NOT implement the guard type, its advisory-lock backends, the sidecar path helper (consumed here), or the stale-break transition wiring (owned by sibling children). Do not change tracker mutation semantics, tracker record format, trackerLockStaleAge, LockRetryPolicy defaults, lockmetrics caps, harness/Fizeau behavior, bead-store locks, git index locks, or the execution-cleanup lock in cli/internal/agent/execution_cleanup_loop.go:116-156. Do not extract a shared lock package; Phase 1 WB-8 owns unification. Do not alter existing .ddx/.git-tracker.lock ignore/exclude behavior beyond adding the sidecar.

PARENT
ddx-1c8d9319

DEPS
Sibling guard-primitive child (crash-safe main-git transition guard primitive with sidecar path helper) — provides the sidecar path helper/constant referenced by all three surfaces.

description:
PROBLEM
Reused attempts need the same combined telemetry inputs as cold-start attempts: slot hit count, slot miss count, time-saved, and bytes-saved. Today the reused-attempt savings values are calculated outside the combined hit/miss telemetry path, so the final reusable workspace event cannot be populated from one execution outcome.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
- `cli/internal/agent/attempt_backend.go:87-110` exposes allocation outcome metadata but does not provide a single reusable-workspace telemetry input that carries both allocation hit/miss state and savings values for reused attempts.
- `cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:985-1052` prepares reusable workspaces and performs cleanup but does not assemble reused allocation outcome data with the savings contract before telemetry emission.
- Attempt-path savings counters are not summarized with hit/miss counters, so reuse wins cannot be observed from one event.

PROPOSED FIX
DEPENDS ON parent `ddx-388ca2af`, parent bead `ddx-940deef7`, parent `ddx-1436e204`, parent `ddx-5dda007b`, child "attempt-backend: expose reusable workspace allocation outcome metadata", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace hit and miss telemetry events", sibling child "attempt-backend: add bounded reusable attempt workspace slot pool with config surface", sibling child "attempt-backend: reuse worktree and local-clone workspaces across sequential attempts with state scrub and quarantine", sibling child "attempt-backend: preserve per-slot Rust build state across beads with toolchain and lock invalidation", child "attempt-backend: calculate reusable workspace savings estimates from allocation outcomes", child "attempt-backend: emit zero reusable workspace savings for cold-start attempts", child "attempt-backend: carry reusable workspace savings through execution telemetry", child "attempt-backend: emit reusable workspace savings for reused attempts", child "attempt-backend: define combined reusable workspace telemetry payload", and child "attempt-backend: emit combined reusable workspace telemetry for cold starts". Add or extend the reusable workspace telemetry input structure so reused attempts carry allocation hit/miss counts together with time-saved and bytes-saved values from the allocation/execution savings contract. Keep the shape compatible with the combined payload used for cold starts.

GOVERNING ARTIFACT
Parent bead `ddx-54ff73df`: attempt-backend combined workspace hit, miss, and savings telemetry.

NON-SCOPE
- Do not share mutable workspaces or Cargo targets between concurrent workers.
- Do not reuse state across projects or trust boundaries.
- Do not weaken attempt isolation, evidence provenance, base-revision correctness, or execution audit history.
- Do not retain secrets, generated evidence, staged changes, untracked source files, or live processes between beads.
- Do not require a global cross-user compilation cache; this bead concerns safe project-local sequential reuse.
- Do not re-implement pool, scrub, quarantine, or build-cache logic delivered by the sibling children.
- Do not change queue claim/release semantics or the Docker attempt backend's existing shared-cache behaviour.
- Do not alter the estimate formula except as needed to consume the contract delivered by the savings-estimate child.
- Do not change the existing Docker attempt backend shared-cache behaviour while adding this event.

1. TestAgentGitConfigEnvSanitizesRepositorySelection proves the shared fixture git helper clears inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` before any fixture `git config` write, while still binding commands to the intended temporary repository.
2. TestAgentGitConfigHelperUsesPrivateConfig proves `core.bare`, `core.worktree`, `user.name`, and `user.email` writes through the fixture helper land only in the temporary fixture repository/config scope and not in the invoking checkout's common config.
3. TestAgentGitConfigHelperFailsClosedWhenPrivateScopeUnavailable proves setup returns a deterministic error before mutation when the helper cannot establish a fixture-private config scope.
4. `cd cli && CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race ./internal/agent/... -run "Test(AgentGitConfigEnvSanitizesRepositorySelection|AgentGitConfigHelperUsesPrivateConfig|AgentGitConfigHelperFailsClosedWhenPrivateScopeUnavailable)" -count=20` passes.
5. `cd cli && go test ./internal/agent/... -timeout 600s` passes.
6. `lefthook run pre-commit` passes.
description:
PROBLEM
Agent tests and fixture helpers that call `git config` can select the invoking checkout's shared common gitdir instead of a temporary fixture repository. When a fixture writes values such as `core.bare=true`, `core.worktree`, `user.name`, or `user.email`, the full agent test suite can corrupt the repository configuration used by the primary checkout and linked worktrees.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_git_isolation.go:20-55 enables worktree config and seeds per-worktree config for execute-bead isolation, and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_git_isolation.go:169-229 wraps commands executed through the agent harness. Fixture setup paths such as runGitInteg/newScriptHarnessRepo are outside that production wrapper and can inherit `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, or common-config selection from the caller, so `git config` can target the shared repository config.

PROPOSED FIX
Introduce or harden a shared helper used by agent test fixtures and subprocess setup so every git invocation that may read or write repository configuration is explicitly bound to the temporary fixture repository or a fixture-private config scope. The helper must clear inherited repository-selection environment (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, and related config selectors as applicable) unless it deliberately sets fixture-local values. Production execute-bead callers must remain wired through the same isolation helper surface instead of growing an ad hoc test-only workaround.

NON-SCOPE
Do not weaken the existing core.bare/core.worktree repair behavior, remove execute-bead config isolation, alter user project Git configuration, or change DDx/Fizeau routing. This child owns helper-level test and execution-isolation correctness only; stale index-lock recovery is ddx-3f156500 and main-git lock safety is ddx-1c8d9319. Parent bead: ddx-8b22914e. Deps: none; independent defect discovered while validating ddx-3f156500.

description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead ddx-9c3e703b is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 3 of 3 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM
Attempt 20260713T094206-53684645 for ddx-415c8b95 had a staged pre-commit gate terminated after it recursively walked 100 leaked host-global module caches. The provider then ran git commit --no-verify and DDx accepted, merged, closed, and pushed implementation commit 85bb0fae0. A code-changing attempt can therefore bypass its required staged hook and still be classified as successful.

ROOT CAUSE WITH FILE:LINE
cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2108-2113 and cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:2143-2148 require tests and a staged lefthook run but do not explicitly forbid --no-verify, hook disabling, or bypassing a failed gate. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go:1507-1514 invokes ValidateAttemptIntegrity without populating GateRuns. cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation.go:160-186 checks gate evidence only when len(GateRuns) is nonzero, and TestValidateAttemptIntegrity_SingleCommitNoEvidenceSkips codifies missing evidence as success. The validation promised by closed bead ddx-725b65b4 is therefore not wired into the live execute-bead path.

PROPOSED FIX
- Add an explicit execute-bead instruction that implementation agents must never use git commit --no-verify, disable hooks, or commit after a required gate failed or was interrupted.
- Capture implementation-agent tool commands and foreground gate outputs/exit codes from the harness session into structured attempt-integrity input.
- When a code-changing bead acceptance requires lefthook run pre-commit, require at least one successful meaningful staged run after the final staged mutation and before the implementation commit. Missing, failed, interrupted, background-only, or no-staged-files evidence must reject and preserve the attempt.
- Treat an implementation-agent git commit --no-verify command as an integrity violation even if a prior gate appeared meaningful.
- Keep DDx-owned checkpoint, tracker-only, landing, and durable-audit commits outside this rule; their scoped --no-verify use is orchestrator-owned.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation.go
- cli/internal/agent/execute_bead_validation_test.go
- execute-bead prompt guardrail/snapshot tests
- nearest harness-session evidence adapter needed to populate GateRuns and implementation commands

NON-SCOPE
Do not rewrite or remove existing execute-bead history, forbid DDx-owned tracker/aud
